        "contents": "def connect_to_db():\n    \"\"\"\n    Establish a connection to the PostgreSQL database.\n    \n    Uses database credentials from environment variables via config.settings.\n    Connection string format: postgresql://user:password@host:port/dbname\n    \n    Returns:\n        psycopg2 connection object if successful, None otherwise\n    \n    Raises:\n        RuntimeError: If psycopg2 is not available\n    \"\"\"\n    if not PSYCOPG2_AVAILABLE:\n        raise RuntimeError(\n            \"psycopg2 library is not available. Please install it using: pip install psycopg2-binary\"\n        )\n    \n    try:\n        # Get database URL from settings\n        settings = get_settings()\n        if settings is None:\n            raise RuntimeError(\"Settings module is not available\")\n        \n        database_url = settings.database_url\n        \n        # Parse the connection string\n        # Format: postgresql://user:password@host:port/dbname\n        parsed = urlparse(database_url)\n        \n        # Extract connection parameters\n        dbname = parsed.path.lstrip('/') if parsed.path else None\n        user = parsed.username\n        password = parsed.password\n        host = parsed.hostname or 'localhost'\n        port = parsed.port or 5432\n        \n        if not dbname or not user or not password:\n            raise ValueError(\n                \"Invalid database URL format. Expected: postgresql://user:password@host:port/dbname\"\n            )\n        \n        # Establish connection\n        conn = psycopg2.connect(\n            dbname=dbname,\n            user=user,\n            password=password,\n            host=host,\n            port=port\n        )\n        \n        return conn\n    \n    except OperationalError as e:\n        print(f\"Error connecting to database: {e}\")\n        return None\n    except (ValueError, AttributeError) as e:\n        print(f\"Error parsing database URL: {e}\")\n        return None\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error connecting to database: {e}\")\n        return None\n\n\ndef create_cloud_metrics_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"",

        "contents": "class Settings:\ndef __init__(self):\n\n        self.ml_min_alert_rate = float(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_MIN_ALERT_RATE\", \"0.50\")\n        )  # Minimum alert rate when anomalies detected (default: 0.50, i.e., 50%)\n        self.ml_performance_lookback_days = int(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_PERFORMANCE_LOOKBACK_DAYS\", \"7\")\n        )  # Days of performance data to analyze (default: 7)\n        self.ml_retraining_threshold_accuracy = float(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_RETRAINING_THRESHOLD_ACCURACY\", \"0.80\")\n        )  # Accuracy threshold for retraining (default: 0.80, for future use with labeled data)\n        \n        self.memory_usage_threshold = float(\n            os.getenv(\"MEMORY_USAGE_THRESHOLD\", \"80.0\")\n        )\n        self.disk_usage_threshold = float(\n            os.getenv(\"DISK_USAGE_THRESHOLD\", \"80.0\")\n        )\n        network_bandwidth_threshold_str = os.getenv(\"NETWORK_BANDWIDTH_THRESHOLD\")\n        if network_bandwidth_threshold_str:\n            self.network_bandwidth_threshold = float(network_bandwidth_threshold_str)\n        else:\n            self.network_bandwidth_threshold = None\n        \n        # Cloud provider settings\n        self.aws_access_key = os.getenv(\"AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID\", \"\")\n        self.aws_secret_key = os.getenv(\"AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY\", \"\")\n        self.aws_region = os.getenv(\"AWS_REGION\", \"us-east-1\")\n        \n        self.azure_subscription_id = os.getenv(\"AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID\", \"\")\n        self.azure_client_id = os.getenv(\"AZURE_CLIENT_ID\", \"\")\n        self.azure_client_secret = os.getenv(\"AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET\", \"\")\n        self.azure_tenant_id = os.getenv(\"AZURE_TENANT_ID\", \"\")\n        \n        self.gcp_project_id = os.getenv(\"GCP_PROJECT_ID\", \"\")\n        self.gcp_credentials_path = os.getenv(\"GCP_CREDENTIALS_PATH\", \"\")\n        \n        # Cloud metrics collection settings\n        self.cloud_metrics_time_window_minutes = int(\n            os.getenv(\"CLOUD_METRICS_TIME_WINDOW_MINUTES\", \"5\")\n        )\n        self.enable_cloud_metrics = os.getenv(\n            \"ENABLE_CLOUD_METRICS\", \"false\"\n        ).lower() == \"true\"\n        self.aws_instance_ids = os.getenv(\"AWS_INSTANCE_IDS\", \"\").strip()\n        self.aws_s3_bucket_names = os.getenv(\"AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAMES\", \"\").strip()\n        self.gcp_instance_names = os.getenv(\"GCP_INSTANCE_NAMES\", \"\").strip()\n        self.gcp_bucket_names = os.getenv(\"GCP_BUCKET_NAMES\", \"\").strip()",

        "contents": "- **Machine Learning**: Optional ML-based detection using Isolation Forest and Autoencoders\n- **Alert Triggering**: Automatic alert generation for detected anomalies\n\n### Policy Management\n- **Policy Definition**: Create and manage monitoring policies\n- **Policy Enforcement**: Automatic policy evaluation and action execution\n- **Flexible Rules**: Support for complex conditions and actions\n\n### Alerting\n- **Multi-Channel**: Email, Slack, and SMS notifications\n- **Alert Logging**: Persistent storage of all alerts\n- **Alert History**: Query and analyze historical alerts\n\n### Self-Healing (Optional)\n- **Auto-Scaling**: Automatic resource scaling based on cost spikes\n- **Service Shutdown**: Graceful shutdown of services when needed\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.11 or higher\n- PostgreSQL 15 or higher\n- Docker and Docker Compose (for containerized deployment)\n- Cloud provider credentials (if using cloud metrics collection)\n\n## Installation\n\n### Local Development Setup\n\n1. **Clone the repository**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   git clone &lt;repository-url&gt;\n   cd monitor_drift_agent\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. **Create virtual environment**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   python -m venv venv\n   source venv/bin/activate  #         "contents": "class Settings:\ndef __init__(self):\n int(\n            os.getenv(\"SUSTAINED_COST_SPIKE_DAYS\", \"3\")\n        )  # Number of consecutive days required to trigger alert (default: 3)\n        \n        # Monitoring control settings\n        self.cost_spike_monitoring_enabled = os.getenv(\n            \"COST_SPIKE_MONITORING_ENABLED\", \"true\"\n        ).lower() == \"true\"  # Enable/disable automatic cost spike monitoring (default: true)\n        self.system_metrics_monitoring_enabled = os.getenv(\n            \"SYSTEM_METRICS_MONITORING_ENABLED\", \"true\"\n        ).lower() == \"true\"  # Enable/disable automatic system metrics monitoring (default: true)\n        \n        # Machine Learning settings\n        self.ml_training_lookback_days = int(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_TRAINING_LOOKBACK_DAYS\", \"30\")\n        )  # Days of historical data for training (default: 30)\n        self.ml_contamination = float(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_CONTAMINATION\", \"0.05\")\n        )  # Expected proportion of anomalies (default: 0.05)\n        self.ml_n_estimators = int(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_N_ESTIMATORS\", \"100\")\n        )  # Number of trees in Isolation Forest (default: 100)\n        self.ml_model_path = os.getenv(\n            \"ML_MODEL_PATH\", \"models/isolation_forest_model.pkl\"\n        )  # Path to save/load trained model\n        self.ml_enabled = os.getenv(\"ML_ENABLED\", \"false\").lower() == \"true\"  # Enable/disable ML-based detection\n        self.ml_anomaly_score_threshold = float(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_ANOMALY_SCORE_THRESHOLD\", \"-0.5\")\n        )  # Anomaly score threshold for alerting (default: -0.5, lower = more anomalous)\n        \n        # ML Retraining settings\n        self.ml_retraining_enabled = os.getenv(\"ML_RETRAINING_ENABLED\", \"false\").lower() == \"true\"  # Enable/disable automatic retraining\n        self.ml_retraining_check_interval_hours = int(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_RETRAINING_CHECK_INTERVAL_HOURS\", \"24\")\n        )  # Hours between performance checks (default: 24)\n        self.ml_min_detection_rate = float(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_MIN_DETECTION_RATE\", \"0.01\")\n        )  # Minimum acceptable detection rate (default: 0.01, i.e., 1%)\n        self.ml_max_detection_rate = float(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_MAX_DETECTION_RATE\", \"0.20\")\n        )  #         "contents": "def create_alerts_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n\n        migration_query = \"\"\"\n        DO $$\n        BEGIN\n            IF NOT EXISTS (\n                SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns \n                WHERE table_name='alerts' AND column_name='severity'\n            ) THEN\n                ALTER TABLE alerts ADD COLUMN severity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium';\n            END IF;\n            \n            IF NOT EXISTS (\n                SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns \n                WHERE table_name='alerts' AND column_name='action_taken'\n            ) THEN\n                ALTER TABLE alerts ADD COLUMN action_taken TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Alert Triggered';\n            END IF;\n        END $$;\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        cursor.execute(migration_query)\n        conn.commit()\n        cursor.close()\n        \n        return True\n    \n    except Error as e:\n        print(f\"Error creating alerts schema: {e}\")\n        if conn:\n            conn.rollback()\n        return False\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error creating alerts schema: {e}\")\n        if conn:\n            conn.rollback()\n        return False\n\n\ndef create_self_healing_log_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Create the database schema for storing self-healing action logs.\n    \n    Creates a table called self_healing_log with columns for resource_name,\n    action_taken, timestamp, cost_at_action, status, and error_message.\n    \n    Args:\n        conn: psycopg2 connection object\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if schema creation successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    if conn is None:\n        print(\"Error: Database connection is None\")\n        return False\n    \n    try:\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        create_table_query = \"\"\"\n        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS self_healing_log (\n            id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n            resource_name TEXT NOT NULL,\n            action_taken TEXT NOT NULL,\n            timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n            cost_at_action NUMERIC,\n            status TEXT,\n            error_message TEXT\n        );\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        cursor.execute(create_table_query)\n        conn.commit()\n        cursor.close()\n        \n        return True\n    \n    except Error as e:\n        print(f\"Error creating self_healing_log schema: {e}\")\n        if conn:\n            conn.rollback()\n        return False\n    except Exception as e:\n        print",

        "contents": "def create_cloud_resource_costs_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n\n    Create the database schema for storing cloud resource cost data.\n    \n    Creates a table called cloud_resource_costs with columns:\n    - id: SERIAL PRIMARY KEY\n    - resource_name: TEXT NOT NULL (e.g., 'AWS EC2', 'S3')\n    - resource_usage: NUMERIC NOT NULL (usage amount)\n    - cost: NUMERIC NOT NULL (calculated cost)\n    - timestamp: TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n    \n    Args:\n        conn: psycopg2 connection object\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if schema creation successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    if conn is None:\n        print(\"Error: Database connection is None\")\n        return False\n    \n    try:\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Create cloud_resource_costs table\n        create_table_query = \"\"\"\n        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cloud_resource_costs (\n            id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n            resource_name TEXT NOT NULL,\n            resource_usage NUMERIC NOT NULL,\n            cost NUMERIC NOT NULL,\n            timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n        );\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        cursor.execute(create_table_query)\n        conn.commit()\n        cursor.close()\n        \n        return True\n    \n    except Error as e:\n        print(f\"Error creating cloud_resource_costs schema: {e}\")\n        if conn:\n            conn.rollback()\n        return False\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error creating cloud_resource_costs schema: {e}\")\n        if conn:\n            conn.rollback()\n        return False\n\n\ndef create_model_performance_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Create the database schema for storing ML model performance metrics.\n    \n    Creates a table called model_performance with columns for tracking\n    model performance metrics such as accuracy, detection rate, and alert rate.\n    \n    Args:\n        conn: psycopg2 connection object\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if schema creation successful, False otherwise\n    ",

        "contents": "def create_alerts_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Create the database schema for storing alerts.\n    \n    Creates a table called alerts with columns for metric_name, value,\n    timestamp, resource_type, severity, and action_taken.\n    Also handles migration for existing tables by adding missing columns.\n    \n    Args:\n        conn: psycopg2 connection object\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if schema creation successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    if conn is None:\n        print(\"Error: Database connection is None\")\n        return False\n    \n    try:\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Create table with new schema (if table doesn't exist)\n        create_table_query = \"\"\"\n        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alerts (\n            id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n            metric_name TEXT NOT NULL,\n            value NUMERIC NOT NULL,\n            timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n            resource_type TEXT NOT NULL,\n            severity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium',\n            action_taken TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Alert Triggered'\n        );\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        cursor.execute(create_table_query)\n        conn.commit()\n        \n        # Migration: Add columns if they don't exist (for existing tables)\n        migration_query = \"\"\"\n        DO $$\n        BEGIN\n            IF NOT EXISTS (\n                SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns \n                WHERE table_name='alerts' AND column_name='severity'\n            ) THEN\n                ALTER TABLE alerts ADD COLUMN severity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium';\n            END IF;\n            \n            IF NOT EXISTS (\n                SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns \n                WHERE table_name='alerts' AND column_name='action_taken'\n            ) THEN\n                ALTER TABLE alerts ADD COLUMN action_taken TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Alert Triggered';\n            END IF;\n        END $$;\n        ",

        "contents": "def check_duplicate_cloud_metric(\n    timestamp: datetime,\n    provider: str,\n    metric_name: str,\n    resource_type: str\n) -&gt; bool:\n\n    \n    try:\n        # Establish database connection\n        conn = connect_to_db()\n        if conn is None:\n            print(\"Failed to establish database connection for duplicate check\")\n            return False\n        \n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Query to check for duplicates in cloud_metrics table\n        # Use a small time window (e.g., 1 second) to account for slight timestamp differences\n        query = \"\"\"\n            SELECT COUNT(*) \n            FROM cloud_metrics \n            WHERE provider = %s \n            AND metric_name = %s \n            AND resource_type = %s \n            AND timestamp &gt;= %s - INTERVAL '1 second'\n            AND timestamp &lt;= %s + INTERVAL '1 second'\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        params = [provider, metric_name, resource_type, timestamp, timestamp]\n        \n        cursor.execute(query, params)\n        count = cursor.fetchone()[0]\n        \n        cursor.close()\n        \n        # Return True if duplicate exists (count &gt; 0)\n        return count &gt; 0\n    \n    except Error as e:\n        print(f\"Error checking for duplicate cloud metric: {e}\")\n        return False\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error checking for duplicate cloud metric: {e}\")\n        return False\n    finally:\n        # Ensure cursor and connection are closed\n        if cursor:\n            cursor.close()\n        if conn:\n            conn.close()\n\n\ndef store_unified_metrics(\n    cpu_usage: float,\n    memory_usage: float,\n    network_traffic: float,\n    resource_type: str,\n    cloud_compute: Optional[float] = None,\n    cloud_storage: Optional[float] = None,\n    cloud_bandwidth: Optional[float] = None,\n    timestamp: Optional[datetime] = None\n) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Store unified metrics (server + cloud) in the cloud_server_metrics table.\n    \n    This function stores both server metrics and optional cloud metrics in\n    a single row in the unified cloud_server_metrics table.\n    \n    Args:\n        cpu_usage: Server CPU usage as percentage (required)\n        memory_usage: Server memory usage as percentage or bytes (required)\n        network_traffic: Server network bandwidth in bytes (required)\n        resource_type: Resource type identifier (Server, AWS, GCP, Azure) (required)\n        cloud_compute: Cloud compute usage (optional)\n        cloud_storage: Cloud storage usage (optional)\n        cloud_bandwidth: Cloud bandwidth usage (optional)\n        timestamp: Timestamp when metrics were collected (optional, defaults to current time)\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if storage successful, False otherwise\n    ",

## Root cause

The default `DATABASE_URL` in `config/settings.py` uses placeholder credentials:
```
postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
```

These don't match your PostgreSQL setup, causing authentication to fail.

## Fixes applied

1. Improved error messages in `connect_to_db()`:
   - Detects password authentication failures
   - Shows which username is being used
   - Provides hints about the correct format

2. Enhanced startup messages in `api/main.py`:
   - Clearer success/failure indicators
   - Instructions on how to fix connection issues
   - Example DATABASE_URL format

3. Better error context in `initialize_database()`:
   - Shows the masked DATABASE_URL being used
   - Provides format guidance

## Solution

Set the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable with your actual PostgreSQL credentials:

**For Windows PowerShell:**
```powershell
$env:DATABASE_URL="postgresql://your_username:your_password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift"
python -m api.main
```

**For Windows CMD:**
```cmd
set DATABASE_URL=postgresql://your_username:your_password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
python -m api.main
```

**Or create a `.env` file** (if you're using python-dotenv):
```
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://your_username:your_password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
```

Replace:
- `your_username` with your PostgreSQL username (e.g., `postgres` or `monitor_drift`)
- `your_password` with your PostgreSQL password
- `localhost:5432` with your PostgreSQL host and port if different
- `monitor_drift` with your database name if different

The API will start even if the database connection fails, but database features won't work until the correct credentials are provided.

        "contents": "# Docker Compose configuration for Monitor/Drift Agent\nversion: '3.8'\n\nservices:\n  # Monitor/Drift Agent service\n  agent:\n    build:\n      context: ..\n      dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile\n    container_name: monitor_drift_agent\n    restart: unless-stopped\n    environment:\n      # Database configuration\n      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://monitor_drift:password@postgres:5432/monitor_drift\n      \n      # Metric collection settings\n      - METRIC_COLLECTION_INTERVAL=60\n      \n      # Threshold settings\n      - DEFAULT_CPU_THRESHOLD=80.0\n      - DEFAULT_MEMORY_THRESHOLD=80.0\n      - DEFAULT_DISK_THRESHOLD=80.0\n      \n      # Cloud provider credentials (set via .env file or secrets)\n      - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}\n      - AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}\n      - AWS_REGION=${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}\n      \n      # Alert channel configuration\n      - EMAIL_SMTP_SERVER=${EMAIL_SMTP_SERVER:-}\n      - EMAIL_SMTP_PORT=${EMAIL_SMTP_PORT:-587}\n      - EMAIL_USERNAME=${EMAIL_USERNAME:-}\n      - EMAIL_PASSWORD=${EMAIL_PASSWORD:-}\n      - SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}\n      \n      # Feature flags\n      - ANOMALY_DETECTION_ENABLED=true\n      - ML_DETECTION_ENABLED=false\n      - SELF_HEALING_ENABLED=false\n      \n      # API settings\n      - API_HOST=0.0.0.0\n      - API_PORT=8000\n      - API_DEBUG=false\n      \n      # Logging\n      - LOG_LEVEL=INFO\n    ports:\n      - \"8000:8000\"\n    volumes:\n      - ../logs:/app/logs\n      - ../data:/app/data\n    depends_on:\n      - postgres\n    networks:\n      - monitor_drift_network\n\n  # PostgreSQL database service\n  postgres:\n    image: postgres:15-alpine",

        "contents": "def connect_to_db():\n    \"\"\"\n    Establish a connection to the PostgreSQL database.\n    \n    Uses database credentials from environment variables via config.settings.\n    Connection string format: postgresql://user:password@host:port/dbname\n    \n    Returns:\n        psycopg2 connection object if successful, None otherwise\n    \n    Raises:\n        RuntimeError: If psycopg2 is not available\n    \"\"\"\n    if not PSYCOPG2_AVAILABLE:\n        raise RuntimeError(\n            \"psycopg2 library is not available. Please install it using: pip install psycopg2-binary\"\n        )\n    \n    try:\n        # Get database URL from settings\n        settings = get_settings()\n        if settings is None:\n            raise RuntimeError(\"Settings module is not available\")\n        \n        database_url = settings.database_url\n        \n        # Parse the connection string\n        # Format: postgresql://user:password@host:port/dbname\n        parsed = urlparse(database_url)\n        \n        # Extract connection parameters\n        dbname = parsed.path.lstrip('/') if parsed.path else None\n        user = parsed.username\n        password = parsed.password\n        host = parsed.hostname or 'localhost'\n        port = parsed.port or 5432\n        \n        if not dbname or not user or not password:\n            raise ValueError(\n                \"Invalid database URL format. Expected: postgresql://user:password@host:port/dbname\"\n            )\n        \n        # Establish connection\n        conn = psycopg2.connect(\n            dbname=dbname,\n            user=user,\n            password=password,\n            host=host,\n            port=port\n        )\n        \n        return conn\n    \n    except OperationalError as e:\n        error_str = str(e)\n        # Provide more helpful error messages\n        if \"password authentication failed\" in error_str.lower():\n            print(f\"Error connecting to database: {error_str}\")\n            print(\"  Hint: Check your DATABASE_URL credentials. Current format: postgresql://username:password@host:port/dbname\")\n            # Try to show the username being used\n            if settings:\n                try:\n                    from urllib.parse import urlparse\n                    parsed = urlparse(settings.database_url)",

        "contents": "\"\"\"\nMain FastAPI application for Monitor/Drift Agent.\n\nThis module creates and configures the FastAPI application,\nincluding all routers and middleware.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import JSONResponse\nfrom fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware\nfrom contextlib import asynccontextmanager\n\n# Try to import slowapi for rate limiting error handling\ntry:\n    from slowapi import Limiter, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler\n    from slowapi.errors import RateLimitExceeded\n    SLOWAPI_AVAILABLE = True\nexcept ImportError:\n    SLOWAPI_AVAILABLE = False\n    RateLimitExceeded = Exception\n\n# Import routers\nfrom api.metrics import router as metrics_router\nfrom api.policies import router as policies_router\n\n# Import settings\ntry:\n    from config.settings import get_settings\nexcept ImportError:\n    def get_settings():\n        return None\n\n\n@asynccontextmanager\nasync def lifespan(app: FastAPI):\n    \"\"\"\n    Lifespan context manager for FastAPI application.\n    \n    Handles startup and shutdown events:\n    - Startup: Initialize database schemas\n    - Shutdown: Cleanup (if needed)\n    \"\"\"\n    # Startup: Initialize database\n    try:\n        from data_collection.database import initialize_database\n        initialized = initialize_database()\n        if initialized:\n            print(\"✓ Database initialized successfully - all schemas created\")\n        else:\n            print(\"⚠ Warning: Database initialization failed or was skipped\")\n            print(\"  The API will start, but database features may not work.\")\n            print(\"  To fix: Set DATABASE_URL environment variable with correct credentials.\")\n            print(\"  Example: export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://username:password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift\")\n    except RuntimeError as e:\n        # psycopg2 not available or other critical error\n        print(f\"✗ Error during database initialization: {e}\")\n        print(\"  The API will start, but database features may not work.\")\n        if \"psycopg2\" in str(e).lower():\n            print(\"  To fix: Install psycopg2-binary: pip install psycopg2-binary\")\n    except Exception as e:\n        # Other errors (connection failures, etc.)\n        print(f\"✗ Error during database initialization: {e}\")\n        print(\"  The API will start, but database features may not work.\")\n        print(\"  To fix: Check your DATABASE_URL environment variable and ensure PostgreSQL is running.\")\n    \n    yield  # Application runs here\n    \n    # Shutdown: Cleanup if needed (none required for now)\n    # Connection cleanup is handled by individual functions\n\n\n# Create FastAPI app\napp = FastAPI(\n    title=\"Monitor/Drift Agent API\",",

        "contents": "async def verify_api_key(\n    x_api_key: Optional[str] = Header(None, alias=\"X-API-KEY\")\n) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Verify API key from request header.\n    \n    Args:\n        x_api_key: API key from X-API-KEY header\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if API key is valid\n    \n    Raises:\n        HTTPException: 401 if API key is missing or invalid when authentication is enabled\n    \"\"\"\n    settings = get_settings()\n    if settings is None:\n        # If settings not available, allow access (fail open for development)\n        return True\n    \n    # Check if API key authentication is enabled\n    if not settings.api_key_enabled:\n        # Authentication is disabled, allow access\n        return True\n    \n    # Authentication is enabled, verify API key\n    if not x_api_key:\n        raise HTTPException(\n            status_code=401,\n            detail=\"API key is required.         "contents": "\"\"\"\nLogging configuration for Monitor/Drift Agent.\n\nThis module provides logging configuration and setup for the application.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport logging\nimport sys\nfrom logging.handlers import RotatingFileHandler\nfrom typing import Optional\n\n\ndef setup_logging(\n    log_level: Optional[str] = None,\n    log_file: Optional[str] = None,\n    log_format: Optional[str] = None\n):\n    \"\"\"\n    Set up logging configuration.\n    \n    Args:\n        log_level: Logging level (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL)\n        log_file: Optional path to log file\n        log_format: Optional custom log format\n    \n    TODO: Implement logging configuration\n    \"\"\"\n    # Get log level from environment or use default\n    level = log_level or os.getenv(\"LOG_LEVEL\", \"INFO\").upper()\n    \n    # Convert string level to logging constant\n    numeric_level = getattr(logging, level, logging.INFO)\n    \n    # Default log format\n    if log_format is None:\n        log_format = (\n            \"%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - \"\n            \"%(filename)s:%(lineno)d - %(message)s\"\n        )\n    \n    # Configure root logger\n    root_logger = logging.getLogger()\n    root_logger.setLevel(numeric_level)\n    \n    # Remove existing handlers\n    root_logger.handlers = []\n    \n    # Console handler\n    console_handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)\n    console_handler.setLevel(numeric_level)\n    console_formatter = logging.Formatter(log_format)\n    console_handler.setFormatter(console_formatter)\n    root_logger.addHandler(console_handler)\n    \n    # File handler (if log file specified)",

        "contents": "- **Machine Learning**: Optional ML-based detection using Isolation Forest and Autoencoders\n- **Alert Triggering**: Automatic alert generation for detected anomalies\n\n### Policy Management\n- **Policy Definition**: Create and manage monitoring policies\n- **Policy Enforcement**: Automatic policy evaluation and action execution\n- **Flexible Rules**: Support for complex conditions and actions\n\n### Alerting\n- **Multi-Channel**: Email, Slack, and SMS notifications\n- **Alert Logging**: Persistent storage of all alerts\n- **Alert History**: Query and analyze historical alerts\n\n### Self-Healing (Optional)\n- **Auto-Scaling**: Automatic resource scaling based on cost spikes\n- **Service Shutdown**: Graceful shutdown of services when needed\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.11 or higher\n- PostgreSQL 15 or higher\n- Docker and Docker Compose (for containerized deployment)\n- Cloud provider credentials (if using cloud metrics collection)\n\n## Installation\n\n### Local Development Setup\n\n1. **Clone the repository**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   git clone &lt;repository-url&gt;\n   cd monitor_drift_agent\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. **Create virtual environment**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   python -m venv venv\n   source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\\Scripts\\activate\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. **Install dependencies**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   # TODO: Create requirements.txt with project dependencies\n   # pip install -r requirements.txt\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. **Set up environment variables**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   # Copy example environment file\n   # cp .env.example .env\n   # Edit .env with your configuration\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n5. **Set up database**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   # Create PostgreSQL database\n   createdb monitor_drift\n   # Run migrations (when implemented)\n   # python -m alembic upgrade head\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Docker Setup\n\n1. **Build and run with Docker Compose**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd docker\n   docker-compose up -d\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. **View logs**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   docker-compose logs -f agent\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. **Stop services**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash",

## Changes made

### 1. Added `.env` file support in `config/settings.py`
- Added automatic loading of `.env` files using `python-dotenv`
- Loads from project root first (`project_root/.env`)
- Falls back to current working directory if not found
- Gracefully handles missing `python-dotenv` (falls back to system environment variables)

### 2. How it works
- If `python-dotenv` is installed: automatically loads `.env` file
- If `python-dotenv` is not installed: uses system environment variables (no error)
- Priority: `.env` file values can override system environment variables

## Usage

1. Install python-dotenv (optional but recommended):
   ```bash
   pip install python-dotenv
   ```

2. Create a `.env` file in the project root (`a:\MonitorDrift Agent\.env`):
   ```env
   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://your_username:your_password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
   ```

3. Run the application:
   ```bash
   python -m api.main
   ```

The application will automatically load variables from the `.env` file.

## Notes

- The `.env` file should be in the project root directory
- If `python-dotenv` is not installed, the app still works but won't load `.env` files
- Environment variables set in the system take precedence (unless `override=True` is used)
- The `.env` file should not be committed to version control (add it to `.gitignore`)

The implementation is backward compatible: if `python-dotenv` isn't installed, it falls back to system environment variables, so existing setups continue to work.

        "contents": "# Docker Compose configuration for Monitor/Drift Agent\nversion: '3.8'\n\nservices:\n  # Monitor/Drift Agent service\n  agent:\n    build:\n      context: ..\n      dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile\n    container_name: monitor_drift_agent\n    restart: unless-stopped\n    environment:\n      # Database configuration\n      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://monitor_drift:password@postgres:5432/monitor_drift\n      \n      # Metric collection settings\n      - METRIC_COLLECTION_INTERVAL=60\n      \n      # Threshold settings\n      - DEFAULT_CPU_THRESHOLD=80.0\n      - DEFAULT_MEMORY_THRESHOLD=80.0\n      - DEFAULT_DISK_THRESHOLD=80.0\n      \n      # Cloud provider credentials (set via .env file or secrets)\n      - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}\n      - AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}\n      - AWS_REGION=${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}\n      \n      # Alert channel configuration\n      - EMAIL_SMTP_SERVER=${EMAIL_SMTP_SERVER:-}\n      - EMAIL_SMTP_PORT=${EMAIL_SMTP_PORT:-587}\n      - EMAIL_USERNAME=${EMAIL_USERNAME:-}\n      - EMAIL_PASSWORD=${EMAIL_PASSWORD:-}\n      - SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}\n      \n      # Feature flags\n      - ANOMALY_DETECTION_ENABLED=true\n      - ML_DETECTION_ENABLED=false\n      - SELF_HEALING_ENABLED=false\n      \n      # API settings\n      - API_HOST=0.0.0.0\n      - API_PORT=8000\n      - API_DEBUG=false\n      \n      # Logging\n      - LOG_LEVEL=INFO\n    ports:\n      - \"8000:8000\"\n    volumes:\n      - ../logs:/app/logs\n      - ../data:/app/data\n    depends_on:\n      - postgres\n    networks:\n      - monitor_drift_network\n\n  # PostgreSQL database service\n  postgres:\n    image: postgres:15-alpine",

        "contents": "- **Machine Learning**: Optional ML-based detection using Isolation Forest and Autoencoders\n- **Alert Triggering**: Automatic alert generation for detected anomalies\n\n### Policy Management\n- **Policy Definition**: Create and manage monitoring policies\n- **Policy Enforcement**: Automatic policy evaluation and action execution\n- **Flexible Rules**: Support for complex conditions and actions\n\n### Alerting\n- **Multi-Channel**: Email, Slack, and SMS notifications\n- **Alert Logging**: Persistent storage of all alerts\n- **Alert History**: Query and analyze historical alerts\n\n### Self-Healing (Optional)\n- **Auto-Scaling**: Automatic resource scaling based on cost spikes\n- **Service Shutdown**: Graceful shutdown of services when needed\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.11 or higher\n- PostgreSQL 15 or higher\n- Docker and Docker Compose (for containerized deployment)\n- Cloud provider credentials (if using cloud metrics collection)\n\n## Installation\n\n### Local Development Setup\n\n1. **Clone the repository**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   git clone &lt;repository-url&gt;\n   cd monitor_drift_agent\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. **Create virtual environment**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   python -m venv venv\n   source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\\Scripts\\activate\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. **Install dependencies**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   # TODO: Create requirements.txt with project dependencies\n   # pip install -r requirements.txt\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. **Set up environment variables**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   # Copy example environment file\n   # cp .env.example .env\n   # Edit .env with your configuration\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n5. **Set up database**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   # Create PostgreSQL database\n   createdb monitor_drift\n   # Run migrations (when implemented)\n   # python -m alembic upgrade head\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Docker Setup\n\n1. **Build and run with Docker Compose**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd docker\n   docker-compose up -d\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. **View logs**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   docker-compose logs -f agent\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. **Stop services**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash",

        "contents": "def create_cloud_metrics_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n\"\"\"\n        \n        cursor.execute(create_table_query)\n        conn.commit()\n        cursor.close()\n        \n        return True\n    \n    except Error as e:\n        print(f\"Error creating cloud metrics schema: {e}\")\n        if conn:\n            conn.rollback()\n        return False\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error creating cloud metrics schema: {e}\")\n        if conn:\n            conn.rollback()\n        return False\n\n\ndef create_alerts_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Create the database schema for storing alerts.\n    \n    Creates a table called alerts with columns for metric_name, value,\n    timestamp, resource_type, severity, and action_taken.\n    Also handles migration for existing tables by adding missing columns.\n    \n    Args:\n        conn: psycopg2 connection object\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if schema creation successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    if conn is None:\n        print(\"Error: Database connection is None\")\n        return False\n    \n    try:\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Create table with new schema (if table doesn't exist)\n        create_table_query = \"\"\"\n        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alerts (\n            id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n            metric_name TEXT NOT NULL,\n            value NUMERIC NOT NULL,\n            timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n            resource_type TEXT NOT NULL,\n            severity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium',\n            action_taken TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Alert Triggered'\n        );\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        cursor.execute(create_table_query)\n        conn.commit()\n        \n        # Migration: Add columns if they don't exist (for existing tables)\n        migration_query = \"\"\"\n        DO $$\n        BEGIN\n            IF NOT EXISTS (\n                SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns \n                WHERE table_name='alerts' AND column_name='severity'\n            ) THEN\n                ALTER TABLE alerts ADD COLUMN severity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium';\n            END IF;\n            \n            IF NOT EXISTS (\n                SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns \n                WHERE table_name='alerts' AND column_name='action_taken'\n            ) THEN\n                ALTER TABLE alerts ADD COLUMN action_taken TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Alert Triggered';\n            END IF;\n        END $$;\n        ",

        "contents": "def check_duplicate_cloud_metric(\n    timestamp: datetime,\n    provider: str,\n    metric_name: str,\n    resource_type: str\n) -&gt; bool:\n\"\"\"\n    Check if a cloud metric with the same timestamp, provider, metric_name, and resource_type already exists.\n    \n    This function queries the cloud_metrics table to check if a record with the same\n    timestamp, provider, metric_name, and resource_type already exists, helping prevent duplicate entries.\n    \n    Args:\n        timestamp: Timestamp to check for duplicates\n        provider: Cloud provider name (aws, gcp, azure)\n        metric_name: Name of the metric\n        resource_type: Resource type (Compute, Storage, Network)\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if duplicate exists, False otherwise\n    \n    Raises:\n        RuntimeError: If psycopg2 is not available\n    \"\"\"\n    if not PSYCOPG2_AVAILABLE:\n        raise RuntimeError(\n            \"psycopg2 library is not available. Please install it using: pip install psycopg2-binary\"\n        )\n    \n    conn = None\n    cursor = None\n    \n    try:\n        # Establish database connection\n        conn = connect_to_db()\n        if conn is None:\n            print(\"Failed to establish database connection for duplicate check\")\n            return False\n        \n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Query to check for duplicates in cloud_metrics table\n        # Use a small time window (e.g., 1 second) to account for slight timestamp differences\n        query = \"\"\"\n            SELECT COUNT(*) \n            FROM cloud_metrics \n            WHERE provider = %s \n            AND metric_name = %s \n            AND resource_type = %s \n            AND timestamp &gt;= %s - INTERVAL '1 second'\n            AND timestamp &lt;= %s + INTERVAL '1 second'\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        params = [provider, metric_name, resource_type, timestamp, timestamp]\n        \n        cursor.execute(query, params)\n        count = cursor.fetchone()[0]\n        \n        cursor.close()\n        \n        # Return True if duplicate exists (count &gt; 0)\n        return count &gt; 0\n    \n    except Error as e:\n        print(f\"Error checking for duplicate cloud metric: {e}\")\n        return False\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error checking for duplicate cloud metric: {e}\")\n        return False\n    finally:\n        # Ensure cursor and connection are closed\n        if cursor:\n            cursor.close()\n        if conn:\n            conn.close()\n\n\ndef store_unified_metrics(\n    cpu_usage: float,\n    memory_usage: float,\n    network_traffic: float,\n    resource_type: str,\n    cloud_compute: Optional[float] = None,\n    cloud_storage: Optional[float] = None,\n    cloud_bandwidth: Optional[float] = None,\n    timestamp: Optional[datetime] = None\n) -&gt; bool:\n    ",

        "contents": "def connect_to_db():\n\n                try:\n                    from urllib.parse import urlparse\n                    parsed = urlparse(settings.database_url)\n                    if parsed.username:\n                        print(f\"  Attempting to connect as user: {parsed.username}\")\n                except Exception:\n                    pass\n        else:\n            print(f\"Error connecting to database: {e}\")\n        return None\n    except (ValueError, AttributeError) as e:\n        print(f\"Error parsing database URL: {e}\")\n        return None\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error connecting to database: {e}\")\n        return None\n\n\ndef create_cloud_metrics_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Create the database schema for storing cloud metrics.\n    \n    Creates a table called cloud_metrics with columns for provider,\n    metric_name, metric_value, timestamp, and resource_type.\n    \n    Args:\n        conn: psycopg2 connection object\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if schema creation successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    if conn is None:\n        print(\"Error: Database connection is None\")\n        return False\n    \n    try:\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Create cloud_metrics table\n        create_table_query = \"\"\"\n        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cloud_metrics (\n            id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n            provider TEXT NOT NULL,\n            metric_name TEXT NOT NULL,\n            metric_value NUMERIC,\n            timestamp TIMESTAMP,\n            resource_type TEXT NOT NULL\n        );\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        cursor.execute(create_table_query)\n        conn.commit()\n        cursor.close()\n        \n        return True",

        "contents": "class Settings:\ndef __init__(self):\n\n        \n        # Cloud provider settings\n        self.aws_access_key = os.getenv(\"AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID\", \"\")\n        self.aws_secret_key = os.getenv(\"AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY\", \"\")\n        self.aws_region = os.getenv(\"AWS_REGION\", \"us-east-1\")\n        \n        self.azure_subscription_id = os.getenv(\"AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID\", \"\")\n        self.azure_client_id = os.getenv(\"AZURE_CLIENT_ID\", \"\")\n        self.azure_client_secret = os.getenv(\"AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET\", \"\")\n        self.azure_tenant_id = os.getenv(\"AZURE_TENANT_ID\", \"\")\n        \n        self.gcp_project_id = os.getenv(\"GCP_PROJECT_ID\", \"\")\n        self.gcp_credentials_path = os.getenv(\"GCP_CREDENTIALS_PATH\", \"\")\n        \n        # Cloud metrics collection settings\n        self.cloud_metrics_time_window_minutes = int(\n            os.getenv(\"CLOUD_METRICS_TIME_WINDOW_MINUTES\", \"5\")\n        )\n        self.enable_cloud_metrics = os.getenv(\n            \"ENABLE_CLOUD_METRICS\", \"false\"\n        ).lower() == \"true\"\n        self.aws_instance_ids = os.getenv(\"AWS_INSTANCE_IDS\", \"\").strip()\n        self.aws_s3_bucket_names = os.getenv(\"AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAMES\", \"\").strip()\n        self.gcp_instance_names = os.getenv(\"GCP_INSTANCE_NAMES\", \"\").strip()\n        self.gcp_bucket_names = os.getenv(\"GCP_BUCKET_NAMES\", \"\").strip()\n        self.azure_vm_names = os.getenv(\"AZURE_VM_NAMES\", \"\").strip()\n        \n        # Alert channel settings\n        self.email_smtp_server = os.getenv(\"EMAIL_SMTP_SERVER\", \"\")\n        self.email_smtp_port = int(os.getenv(\"EMAIL_SMTP_PORT\", \"587\"))\n        self.email_username = os.getenv(\"EMAIL_USERNAME\", \"\")\n        self.email_password = os.getenv(\"EMAIL_PASSWORD\", \"\")\n        email_recipients_str = os.getenv(\"EMAIL_RECIPIENTS\", \"\")\n        self.email_recipients = [r.strip() for r in email_recipients_str.split(\",\") if r.strip()] if email_recipients_str else []\n        self.email_use_sendgrid = os.getenv(\"EMAIL_USE_SENDGRID\", \"false\").lower() == \"true\"\n        self.sendgrid_api_key = os.getenv(\"SENDGRID_API_KEY\", \"\")\n        \n        self.slack_webhook_url = os.getenv(\"SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL\", \"\")\n        \n        self.sms_api_key = os.getenv(\"SMS_API_KEY\", \"\")\n        self.sms_api_secret = os.getenv(\"SMS_API_SECRET\", \"\")\n        self.sms_from_number = os.getenv(\"SMS_FROM_NUMBER\", \"\")\n        self.sms_use_twilio = os.getenv(\"SMS_USE_TWILIO\", \"true\").lower() == \"true\"\n        self.sms_api_url = os.getenv(\"SMS_API_URL\", \"\")\n        self.sms_api_method = os.getenv(\"SMS_API_METHOD\", \"POST\")\n        \n        # Alert preferences\n        self.alert_preferences = self._parse_alert_preferences()",

        "contents": "# Dockerfile for Monitor/Drift Agent\n# Multi-stage build for optimized image size\n\n# Stage 1: Build stage\nFROM python:3.11-slim as builder\n\n# Set working directory\nWORKDIR /app\n\n# Install build dependencies\nRUN apt-get update &amp;&amp; apt-get install -y \\\n    gcc \\\n    g++ \\\n    postgresql-client \\\n    &amp;&amp; rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*\n\n# Copy requirements file (if exists)\n# TODO: Create requirements.txt with project dependencies\n# COPY requirements.txt .\n\n# Install Python dependencies\n# TODO: Uncomment when requirements.txt is available\n# RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --user -r requirements.txt\n\n# Stage 2: Runtime stage\nFROM python:3.11-slim\n\n# Set working directory\nWORKDIR /app\n\n# Install runtime dependencies\nRUN apt-get update &amp;&amp; apt-get install -y \\\n    postgresql-client \\\n    curl \\\n    &amp;&amp; rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*\n\n# Copy Python dependencies from builder\n# TODO: Uncomment when requirements are installed\n# COPY --from=builder /root/.local /root/.local\n\n# Copy application code\nCOPY . .\n\n# Make sure scripts in .local are usable\nENV PATH=/root/.local/bin:$PATH\n\n# Set Python path\nENV PYTHONPATH=/app\n\n# Create non-root user for security\nRUN useradd -m -u 1000 agent &amp;&amp; \\\n    chown -R agent:agent /app\n\n# Switch to non-root user\nUSER agent\n\n# Expose API port\nEXPOSE 8000\n\n# Health check\nHEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \\\n    CMD curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1\n\n# Use entrypoint script\nENTRYPOINT [\"/app/docker/entrypoint.sh\"]\n\n# Default command\nCMD [\"python\", \"-m\", \"api\"]",

        "contents": "\"\"\"\nLogic for logging alerts in the database.\n\nThis module provides functionality to log alerts to the database\nfor persistence and historical tracking.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom typing import Dict, List, Optional\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\n\nclass AlertLogger:\n    \"\"\"Handles logging of alerts to the database.\"\"\"\n    \n    def __init__(self, database=None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize alert logger.\n        \n        Args:\n            database: Optional database connection for logging\n        \"\"\"\n        self.database = database\n    \n    def log_alert(self, alert: Dict) -&gt; str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Log an alert to the database.\n        \n        Args:\n            alert: Dictionary containing alert information\n        \n        Returns:\n            Alert ID of logged alert\n        \n        TODO: Implement alert logging to database\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self.database:\n            # TODO: Log warning that database is not available\n            return \"\"\n        \n        # TODO: Prepare alert data for database insertion\n        alert_data = {\n            \"alert_id\": alert.get(\"alert_id\"),\n            \"alert_type\": alert.get(\"alert_type\"),\n            \"severity\": alert.get(\"severity\"),\n            \"message\": alert.get(\"message\"),\n            \"metadata\": alert.get(\"metadata\", {}),\n            \"status\": alert.get(\"status\", \"created\"),\n            \"created_at\": alert.get(\"timestamp\", datetime.now().isoformat()),\n            \"channels\": alert.get(\"channels\", {})\n        }\n        \n        # TODO: Insert alert into database\n        alert_id = self.database.insert_alert(alert_data)\n        \n        return alert_id\n    \n    def log_alert_batch(self, alerts: List[Dict]) -&gt; List[str]:\n        \"\"\"",

How to get your `DATABASE_URL`:

## DATABASE_URL format

The format is:
```
postgresql://username:password@host:port/database_name
```

## How to get your DATABASE_URL

### Scenario 1: Local PostgreSQL installation

1. Find your PostgreSQL credentials:
   - Username: usually `postgres` (default superuser) or a custom user
   - Password: set during PostgreSQL installation
   - Host: `localhost` (if local) or the server IP
   - Port: `5432` (default PostgreSQL port)
   - Database name: create one or use an existing one

2. Create the database (if needed):
   ```bash
   # Connect to PostgreSQL
   psql -U postgres
   
   # Create database
   CREATE DATABASE monitor_drift;
   
   # Create user (optional)
   CREATE USER monitor_drift WITH PASSWORD 'your_password';
   GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE monitor_drift TO monitor_drift;
   ```

3. Construct your DATABASE_URL:
   ```
   postgresql://postgres:your_password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
   ```

### Scenario 2: Using Docker Compose (from your project)

If you're using the Docker setup in your project:

From `docker-compose.yml`, the database is configured as:
- Username: `monitor_drift`
- Password: `password`
- Database: `monitor_drift`
- Host: `postgres` (inside Docker network) or `localhost` (from host machine)
- Port: `5432`

For Docker Compose (inside containers):
```
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://monitor_drift:password@postgres:5432/monitor_drift
```

For local access (from your host machine):
```
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://monitor_drift:password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
```

### Scenario 3: Cloud PostgreSQL (AWS RDS, Azure, GCP, etc.)

Get the connection details from your cloud provider's console:
- Host: provided by the cloud provider (e.g., `mydb.xxxxx.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com`)
- Port: usually `5432`
- Username: your database username
- Password: your database password
- Database: your database name

Example:
```
postgresql://username:password@mydb.xxxxx.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com:5432/monitor_drift
```

## Quick steps to find your credentials

### Method 1: Check if PostgreSQL is running locally
```bash
# Windows (PowerShell)
Get-Service -Name postgresql*

# Or check if port 5432 is in use
netstat -an | findstr 5432
```

### Method 2: Try connecting with psql
```bash
# Try default connection
psql -U postgres

# Or with specific user
psql -U your_username -d postgres
```

### Method 3: Check PostgreSQL configuration
- Windows: Check `C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\[version]\data\pg_hba.conf`
- Or check your PostgreSQL installation documentation

## Setting up your .env file

1. Create `.env` in your project root (`a:\MonitorDrift Agent\.env`):
   ```env
   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://your_username:your_password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
   ```

2. Replace the placeholders:
   - `your_username` → your PostgreSQL username
   - `your_password` → your PostgreSQL password
   - `localhost` → your database host (use `postgres` if using Docker)
   - `5432` → your PostgreSQL port (default is 5432)
   - `monitor_drift` → your database name

## Example configurations

### Default local PostgreSQL:
```env
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:mypassword@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
```

### Docker Compose (from host):
```env
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://monitor_drift:password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
```

### Docker Compose (from container):
```env
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://monitor_drift:password@postgres:5432/monitor_drift
```

### With special characters in password:
If your password contains special characters, URL-encode them:
```env
# Password: my@pass#word
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:my%40pass%23word@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
```

## Testing your DATABASE_URL

After setting it, test the connection:
```bash
python -m api.main
```

You should see:
```
✓ Database initialized successfully - all schemas created
```

If you see an error, check:
1. PostgreSQL is running
2. Username and password are correct
3. Database exists
4. Host and port are correct
5. Firewall allows the connection

Need help finding your specific PostgreSQL credentials? Share your setup (local, Docker, or cloud) and I can provide more specific steps.

Easiest way to test: use Docker to run PostgreSQL. Two options:

Option 1: Single Docker command (fastest)
Run this in PowerShell:


---

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="read_file_v2">
<details><summary>Tool use: **read_file_v2** • Read file: a:\MonitorDrift Agent\config\settings.py</summary>

## Easiest method: Docker PostgreSQL (recommended)

### Step 1: Start PostgreSQL with Docker

Run this in PowerShell:

```powershell
docker run -d `
  --name monitor_drift_postgres `
  -e POSTGRES_DB=monitor_drift `
  -e POSTGRES_USER=monitor_drift `
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=password `
  -p 5432:5432 `
  postgres:15-alpine
```

This will:
- Download PostgreSQL (first time only)
- Create a database named `monitor_drift`
- Create user `monitor_drift` with password `password`
- Expose port 5432 on your localhost

### Step 2: Create `.env` file

Create a file named `.env` in your project root (`a:\MonitorDrift Agent\.env`) with this content:

```env
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://monitor_drift:password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
```

### Step 3: Install python-dotenv (if not already installed)

```powershell
pip install python-dotenv
```

### Step 4: Test the connection

```powershell
python -m api.main
```

You should see:
```
✓ Database initialized successfully - all schemas created
```

---

## Alternative: Use Docker Compose (if you prefer)

If you want to use the existing docker-compose setup:

### Step 1: Start only the PostgreSQL service

```powershell
cd docker
docker-compose up -d postgres
```

### Step 2: Create `.env` file

Same as above - create `.env` in project root:
```env
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://monitor_drift:password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
```

### Step 3: Test

```powershell
python -m api.main
```

---

## Quick verification

Check if PostgreSQL is running:
```powershell
docker ps
```

You should see `monitor_drift_postgres` in the list.

Check the logs:
```powershell
docker logs monitor_drift_postgres
```

---

## Stop the database (when done testing)

```powershell
docker stop monitor_drift_postgres
docker rm monitor_drift_postgres
```

Or if using docker-compose:
```powershell
cd docker
docker-compose down
```

---

## Summary

1. Run the Docker command above
2. Create `.env` file with the DATABASE_URL
3. Run `pip install python-dotenv` (if needed)
4. Run `python -m api.main`

The database will be automatically initialized with all required tables when the API starts.

Solution 2: Install Docker Desktop (if not installed)

---


### Option A: Install PostgreSQL on Windows

1. Download PostgreSQL:
   - Go to: https://www.postgresql.org/download/windows/
   - Or use the installer: https://www.enterprisedb.com/downloads/postgres-postgresql-downloads
   - Download the Windows installer

2. Install PostgreSQL:
   - Run the installer
   - Remember the password you set for the `postgres` user
   - Keep the default port `5432`
   - Complete the installation

3. Create the database:
   - Open "SQL Shell (psql)" from the Start menu
   - Press Enter for all defaults (host, port, database, username)
   - Enter the password you set during installation
   - Run these commands:
   ```sql
   CREATE DATABASE monitor_drift;
   CREATE USER monitor_drift WITH PASSWORD 'password';
   GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE monitor_drift TO monitor_drift;
   \q
   ```

4. Create `.env` file:
   Create `a:\MonitorDrift Agent\.env` with:
   ```env
   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:YOUR_POSTGRES_PASSWORD@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
   ```
   Replace `YOUR_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` with the password you set during installation.

5. Test:
   ```powershell
   python -m api.main
   ```

---

## Quick decision guide

- Use Docker if: you want a quick, isolated setup and can start Docker Desktop.
- Use local PostgreSQL if: you prefer a permanent installation or don't want to use Docker.

---

## Recommended: Fix Docker Desktop

1. Check if Docker Desktop is installed:
   ```powershell
   Get-Command docker
   ```
   - If it shows a path, Docker is installed but not running.
   - If it says "not found", Docker is not installed.

2. If installed but not running:
   - Open Docker Desktop from Start menu
   - Wait for it to fully start (whale icon in system tray)
   - Try `docker ps` again

3. If not installed:
   - Download: https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/
   - Install and restart your computer
   - Start Docker Desktop

---

## Quick test after fixing Docker

Once Docker is running, test with:
```powershell
docker run hello-world
```

If this works, you can proceed with the PostgreSQL setup I mentioned earlier.

Which option do you prefer? I can provide more detailed steps for either Docker or local PostgreSQL.

        "contents": "class CustomLogger:\n\n    \n    def warning(self, message: str, **kwargs):\n        \"\"\"Log warning message.\"\"\"\n        self.logger.warning(self._format_message(message), **kwargs)\n    \n    def error(self, message: str, **kwargs):\n        \"\"\"Log error message.\"\"\"\n        self.logger.error(self._format_message(message), **kwargs)\n    \n    def critical(self, message: str, **kwargs):\n        \"\"\"Log critical message.\"\"\"\n        self.logger.critical(self._format_message(message), **kwargs)\n    \n    def log_metric(self, metric_name: str, value: float, **metadata):\n        \"\"\"\n        Log a metric with structured data.\n        \n        Args:\n            metric_name: Name of the metric\n            value: Metric value\n            **metadata: Additional metadata\n        \"\"\"\n        message = f\"Metric: {metric_name}={value}\"\n        if metadata:\n            metadata_str = \" | \".join([f\"{k}={v}\" for k, v in metadata.items()])\n            message = f\"{message} | {metadata_str}\"\n        self.info(message)\n    \n    def log_alert(self, alert_type: str, severity: str, message: str, **metadata):\n        \"\"\"\n        Log an alert with structured data.\n        \n        Args:\n            alert_type: Type of alert\n            severity: Alert severity\n            message: Alert message\n            **metadata: Additional metadata\n        \"\"\"\n        log_message = f\"Alert [{severity.upper()}] {alert_type}: {message}\"\n        if metadata:\n            metadata_str = \" | \".join([f\"{k}={v}\" for k, v in metadata.items()])\n            log_message = f\"{log_message} | {metadata_str}\"\n        \n        # Use appropriate log level based on severity\n        severity_levels = {\n            \"low\": self.info,\n            \"medium\": self.warning,\n            \"high\": self.error,\n            \"critical\": self.critical\n        }\n        log_func = severity_levels.get(severity.lower(), self.warning)\n        log_func(log_message)\n\n\ndef get_logger(name: str) -&gt; CustomLogger:\n    \"\"\"",

        "contents": "\"\"\"\nLogic for logging alerts in the database.\n\nThis module provides functionality to log alerts to the database\nfor persistence and historical tracking.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom typing import Dict, List, Optional\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\n\nclass AlertLogger:\n    \"\"\"Handles logging of alerts to the database.\"\"\"\n    \n    def __init__(self, database=None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize alert logger.\n        \n        Args:\n            database: Optional database connection for logging\n        \"\"\"\n        self.database = database\n    \n    def log_alert(self, alert: Dict) -&gt; str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Log an alert to the database.\n        \n        Args:\n            alert: Dictionary containing alert information\n        \n        Returns:\n            Alert ID of logged alert\n        \n        TODO: Implement alert logging to database\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self.database:\n            # TODO: Log warning that database is not available\n            return \"\"\n        \n        # TODO: Prepare alert data for database insertion\n        alert_data = {\n            \"alert_id\": alert.get(\"alert_id\"),\n            \"alert_type\": alert.get(\"alert_type\"),\n            \"severity\": alert.get(\"severity\"),\n            \"message\": alert.get(\"message\"),\n            \"metadata\": alert.get(\"metadata\", {}),\n            \"status\": alert.get(\"status\", \"created\"),\n            \"created_at\": alert.get(\"timestamp\", datetime.now().isoformat()),\n            \"channels\": alert.get(\"channels\", {})\n        }\n        \n        # TODO: Insert alert into database\n        alert_id = self.database.insert_alert(alert_data)\n        \n        return alert_id\n    \n    def log_alert_batch(self, alerts: List[Dict]) -&gt; List[str]:\n        \"\"\"",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

        "contents": "def monitor_cost_spikes_and_trigger_alerts():\n    \"\"\"\n    Monitor cloud costs and automatically detect spikes, triggering alerts.\n    \n    This function addresses the pain point of unforeseen costs by:\n    1.         "contents": "def monitor_cost_spikes_and_trigger_alerts():\n\"\"\"\n    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n    \n    try:\n        # Import required modules\n        from data_collection.cloud_metrics import get_cloud_costs\n        from anomaly_detection.threshold_detection import (\n            compare_cost_to_historical,\n            monitor_sustained_spikes,\n            check_thresholds\n        )\n        from config.settings import get_settings\n        \n        settings = get_settings()\n        if settings is None:\n            logger.warning(\"Settings not available, skipping cost spike monitoring\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'error': 'Settings not available'}\n        \n        # Check if cost spike monitoring is enabled\n        cost_monitoring_enabled = getattr(settings, 'cost_spike_monitoring_enabled', True)\n        if not cost_monitoring_enabled:\n            logger.debug(\"Cost spike monitoring disabled in settings\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'skipped': 'Monitoring disabled'}\n        \n        if not settings.enable_cloud_metrics:\n            logger.debug(\"Cloud metrics disabled, skipping cost spike monitoring\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'skipped': 'Cloud metrics disabled'}\n        \n        logger.info(\"Starting cost spike monitoring and alert detection...\")\n        \n        # Collect real-time cloud costs\n        try:\n            cloud_cost_data = get_cloud_costs(store_in_db=True)\n            cost_items = cloud_cost_data.get('cloud_cost', [])\n            total_cost = cloud_cost_data.get('total_cost', 0.0)\n            \n            if not cost_items:\n                logger.debug(\"No cloud cost data collected, skipping spike detection\")\n                return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'skipped': 'No cost data'}\n            \n            logger.info(f\"Collected {len(cost_items)} cloud cost items. Total cost: ${total_cost:.2f}\")\n            \n        except Exception as e:\n            logger.error(f\"Failed to collect cloud costs: {e}\", exc_info=True)\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'error': str(e)}\n        \n        # Monitor each resource for cost spikes\n        alerts_triggered = 0",

        "contents": "class Settings:\ndef __init__(self):\n(\n            os.getenv(\"DEFAULT_MEMORY_THRESHOLD\", \"80.0\")\n        )\n        self.default_disk_threshold = float(\n            os.getenv(\"DEFAULT_DISK_THRESHOLD\", \"80.0\")\n        )\n        \n        # minutes\n        self.cloud_cost_threshold = float(\n            os.getenv(\"CLOUD_COST_THRESHOLD\", \"500.0\")\n        )  # dollars per day\n        self.cost_spike_threshold_percent = float(\n            os.getenv(\"COST_SPIKE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT\", \"20.0\")\n        )  #         "contents": "- **Machine Learning**: Optional ML-based detection using Isolation Forest and Autoencoders\n- **Alert Triggering**: Automatic alert generation for detected anomalies\n\n### Policy Management\n- **Policy Definition**: Create and manage monitoring policies\n- **Policy Enforcement**: Automatic policy evaluation and action execution\n- **Flexible Rules**: Support for complex conditions and actions\n\n### Alerting\n- **Multi-Channel**: Email, Slack, and SMS notifications\n- **Alert Logging**: Persistent storage of all alerts\n- **Alert History**: Query and analyze historical alerts\n\n### Self-Healing (Optional)\n- **Auto-Scaling**: Automatic resource scaling based on cost spikes\n- **Service Shutdown**: Graceful shutdown of services when needed\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.11 or higher\n- PostgreSQL 15 or higher\n- Docker and Docker Compose (for containerized deployment)\n- Cloud provider credentials (if using cloud metrics collection)\n\n## Installation\n\n### Local Development Setup\n\n1. **Clone the repository**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   git clone &lt;repository-url&gt;\n   cd monitor_drift_agent\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. **Create virtual environment**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   python -m venv venv\n   source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\\Scripts\\activate\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. **Install dependencies**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   # TODO: Create requirements.txt with project dependencies\n   # pip install -r requirements.txt\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. **Set up environment variables**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   # Copy example environment file\n   # cp .env.example .env\n   # Edit .env with your configuration\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n5. **Set up database**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   # Create PostgreSQL database\n   createdb monitor_drift\n   # Run migrations (when implemented)\n   # python -m alembic upgrade head\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Docker Setup\n\n1. **Build and run with Docker Compose**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd docker\n   docker-compose up -d\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. **View logs**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   docker-compose logs -f agent\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. **Stop services**\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash",

        "contents": "def get_server_metrics() -&gt; Dict:\n\n    except Exception as e:\n        raise RuntimeError(f\"Failed to collect server metrics: {str(e)}\")\n\n\ndef collect_and_store_metrics() -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Collect system metrics and store them in the database.\n    \n    This function collects CPU, memory, and network metrics using\n    the individual collection functions and stores them in PostgreSQL.\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if collection and storage successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        # Import here to avoid circular dependencies\n        from data_collection.database import store_metrics\n        from utils.logger import get_logger\n        \n        logger = get_logger(__name__)\n        \n        # Collect all metrics\n        logger.info(\"Collecting system metrics...\")\n        cpu_data = get_cpu_usage()\n        memory_data = get_memory_usage()\n        network_data = get_network_traffic()\n        \n        # Store metrics in database\n        logger.info(\"Storing metrics in database...\")\n        success = store_metrics(cpu_data, memory_data, network_data)\n        \n        if success:\n            logger.info(\"Metrics collected and stored successfully\")\n        else:\n            logger.error(\"Failed to store metrics in database\")\n        \n        return success\n    \n    except RuntimeError as e:\n        # Handle errors from metric collection (e.g., psutil not available)\n        try:\n            from utils.logger import get_logger\n            logger = get_logger(__name__)\n            logger.error(f\"Failed to collect metrics: {str(e)}\")\n        except ImportError:\n            print(f\"Failed to collect metrics: {str(e)}\")\n        return False\n    \n    except Exception as e:\n        # Handle any other unexpected errors\n        try:\n            from utils.logger import get_logger\n            logger = get_logger(__name__)\n            logger.error(f\"Unexpected error during metric collection: {str(e)}\", exc_info=True)\n        except ImportError:\n            print(f\"Unexpected error during metric collection: {str(e)}\")\n        return False\n\n\ndef collect_all_metrics() -&gt; Dict:\n    \"\"\"",

Server metrics (CPU usage, memory usage)\n    - Cloud metrics (AWS, GCP, Azure)\n    \n    Returns:\n        Dictionary containing:\n            - timestamp: str (ISO format timestamp when collection started)\n            - server_metrics: Dict (CPU and memory usage with timestamp)\n            - cloud_metrics: Dict (AWS, GCP, Azure metrics by provider)\n    \n    Errors are handled gracefully - if a cloud provider is not configured\n    or fails, it will be omitted from results rather than causing failure.\n    \"\"\"\n    from utils.logger import get_logger\n    logger = get_logger(__name__)\n    \n    # Capture collection start timestamp (UTC)\n    collection_timestamp = datetime.utcnow()\n    \n    # Initialize result structure\n    result = {\n        'timestamp': collection_timestamp.isoformat(),\n        'server_metrics': {},\n        'cloud_metrics': {}\n    }\n    \n    # Collect server metrics\n    try:\n        result['server_metrics'] = get_server_metrics()\n        logger.info(\"Server metrics collected successfully\")\n    except RuntimeError as e:\n        logger.error(f\"Failed to collect server metrics: {str(e)}\")\n        result['server_metrics'] = {'error': str(e)}\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.error(f\"Unexpected error collecting server metrics: {str(e)}\", exc_info=True)\n        result['server_metrics'] = {'error': str(e)}\n    \n    # Collect cloud metrics - Enable/disable ML-based detection\n        self.ml_anomaly_score_threshold = float(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_ANOMALY_SCORE_THRESHOLD\", \"-0.5\")\n        )  # Anomaly score threshold for alerting (default: -0.5, lower = more anomalous)\n        \n        # ML Retraining settings\n        self.ml_retraining_enabled = os.getenv(\"ML_RETRAINING_ENABLED\", \"false\").lower() == \"true\"  # Enable/disable automatic retraining\n        self.ml_retraining_check_interval_hours = int(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_RETRAINING_CHECK_INTERVAL_HOURS\", \"24\")\n        )  # Hours between performance checks (default: 24)\n        self.ml_min_detection_rate = float(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_MIN_DETECTION_RATE\", \"0.01\")\n        )  # Minimum acceptable detection rate (default: 0.01, i.e., 1%)\n        self.ml_max_detection_rate = float(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_MAX_DETECTION_RATE\", \"0.20\")\n        )  # Maximum acceptable detection rate (default: 0.20, i.e., 20%)\n        self.ml_min_alert_rate = float(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_MIN_ALERT_RATE\", \"0.50\")\n        )  # Minimum alert rate when anomalies detected (default: 0.50, i.e., 50%)\n        self.ml_performance_lookback_days = int(\n            os.getenv(\"ML_PERFORMANCE_LOOKBACK_DAYS\", \"7\")\n        )  # ## Implementation complete

### What was created

1. Error-only log file: `logs/errors.log`
   - Location: `a:\MonitorDrift Agent\logs\errors.log`
   - Only stores ERROR and CRITICAL level messages
   - Automatically created when the application starts

2. Automatic error capture:
   - All ERROR and CRITICAL logs from the logging system
   - Unhandled exceptions (via `sys.excepthook`)
   - Terminal/stderr errors containing keywords: "error", "exception", "traceback", "failed" (with connection/authentication)

3. Features:
   - Rotating file handler (10MB max, 10 backups)
   - Preserves error handler when logging is reconfigured
   - Prevents duplicate handlers
   - Creates logs directory automatically

### How it works

When you run the application:
```powershell
python -m api.main
```

All errors are automatically captured and stored in:
```
a:\MonitorDrift Agent\logs\errors.log
```

### Error log format

Each error entry includes:
- Timestamp
- Logger name
- Log level (ERROR/CRITICAL)
- Filename and line number
- Error message
- Full traceback (for exceptions)

### Example error log entry

```
2026-01-15 18:30:45,123 - data_collection.database - ERROR - database.py:304 - Error connecting to database: connection to server at "localhost" (::1), port 5432 failed: FATAL:  password authentication failed for user "user"
```

The error log file is created automatically and errors are captured without any additional code changes.

_**Agent (model grok-code-fast-1, mode Ask)**_


This error means Docker Desktop isn't running or isn't installed.

## What the error means

The error:
```
failed to connect to the docker API at npipe:////./pipe/dockerDesktopLinuxEngine
```

Indicates:
- Docker Desktop isn't running, or
- Docker Desktop isn't installed

The `npipe:////./pipe/dockerDesktopLinuxEngine` path is the Windows named pipe Docker Desktop uses. If it's missing, Docker Desktop isn't running.

## How to fix

### Option 1: Start Docker Desktop (if installed)

1. Open Docker Desktop from the Start menu.
2. Wait until it shows "Docker Desktop is running" in the system tray.
3. Verify:
   ```powershell
   docker ps
   ```
   If it works, Docker is running.

### Option 2: Install Docker Desktop (if not installed)

1. Download: https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/
2. Install and restart your computer.
3. Start Docker Desktop and wait until it's running.
4. Verify:
   ```powershell
   docker --version
   ```

## Alternative: Use local PostgreSQL (no Docker)

If you don't want to use Docker, install PostgreSQL locally:

1. Download PostgreSQL for Windows:
   - https://www.postgresql.org/download/windows/
   - Or: https://www.enterprisedb.com/downloads/postgres-postgresql-downloads

2. Install PostgreSQL:
   - Run the installer
   - Remember the password you set for the `postgres` user
   - Keep default port `5432`

3. Create the database:
   - Open "SQL Shell (psql)" from Start menu
   - Press Enter for defaults
   - Enter your PostgreSQL password
   - Run:
   ```sql
   CREATE DATABASE monitor_drift;
   CREATE USER monitor_drift WITH PASSWORD 'password';
   GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE monitor_drift TO monitor_drift;
   \q
   ```

4. Create `.env` file in project root:
   ```env
   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:YOUR_PASSWORD@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
   ```
   Replace `YOUR_PASSWORD` with the password you set during installation.

5. Test:
   ```powershell
   python -m api.main
   ```

## Quick check

To see if Docker is installed:
```powershell
Get-Command docker
```

- If it shows a path: Docker is installed but not running → Start Docker Desktop
- If it says "not found": Docker is not installed → Install Docker Desktop or use local PostgreSQL

Which option do you prefer: fix Docker Desktop, or install PostgreSQL locally?

        "contents": "def get_server_metrics() -&gt; Dict:\n\n    except Exception as e:\n        raise RuntimeError(f\"Failed to collect server metrics: {str(e)}\")\n\n\ndef collect_and_store_metrics() -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Collect system metrics and store them in the database.\n    \n    This function collects CPU, memory, and network metrics using\n    the individual collection functions and stores them in PostgreSQL.\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if collection and storage successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        # Import here to avoid circular dependencies\n        from data_collection.database import store_metrics\n        from utils.logger import get_logger\n        \n        logger = get_logger(__name__)\n        \n        # Collect all metrics\n        logger.info(\"Collecting system metrics...\")\n        cpu_data = get_cpu_usage()\n        memory_data = get_memory_usage()\n        network_data = get_network_traffic()\n        \n        # Store metrics in database\n        logger.info(\"Storing metrics in database...\")\n        success = store_metrics(cpu_data, memory_data, network_data)\n        \n        if success:\n            logger.info(\"Metrics collected and stored successfully\")\n        else:\n            logger.error(\"Failed to store metrics in database\")\n        \n        return success\n    \n    except RuntimeError as e:\n        # Handle errors from metric collection (e.g., psutil not available)\n        try:\n            from utils.logger import get_logger\n            logger = get_logger(__name__)\n            logger.error(f\"Failed to collect metrics: {str(e)}\")\n        except ImportError:\n            print(f\"Failed to collect metrics: {str(e)}\")\n        return False\n    \n    except Exception as e:\n        # Handle any other unexpected errors\n        try:\n            from utils.logger import get_logger\n            logger = get_logger(__name__)\n            logger.error(f\"Unexpected error during metric collection: {str(e)}\", exc_info=True)\n        except ImportError:\n            print(f\"Unexpected error during metric collection: {str(e)}\")\n        return False\n\n\ndef collect_all_metrics() -&gt; Dict:\n    \"\"\"",

        "contents": "def connect_to_db():\n    \"\"\"\n    Establish a connection to the PostgreSQL database.\n    \n    Uses database credentials from environment variables via config.settings.\n    Connection string format: postgresql://user:password@host:port/dbname\n    \n    Returns:\n        psycopg2 connection object if successful, None otherwise\n    \n    Raises:\n        RuntimeError: If psycopg2 is not available\n    \"\"\"\n    if not PSYCOPG2_AVAILABLE:\n        raise RuntimeError(\n            \"psycopg2 library is not available.
