Expected: postgresql://user:password@host:port/dbname\"\n            )\n        \n        # Establish connection\n        conn = psycopg2.connect(\n            dbname=dbname,\n            user=user,\n            password=password,\n            host=host,\n            port=port\n        )\n        \n        return conn\n    \n    except OperationalError as e:\n        error_str = str(e)\n        # Provide more helpful error messages\n        if \"password authentication failed\" in error_str.lower():\n            print(f\"Error connecting to database: {error_str}\")\n            print(\"  Hint: Check your DATABASE_URL credentials.         "contents": "\"\"\"\nLogging configuration for Monitor/Drift Agent.\n\nThis module provides logging configuration and setup for the application.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport logging\nimport sys\nfrom logging.handlers import RotatingFileHandler\nfrom typing import Optional\n\n# Initialize error capture early to catch all terminal errors\ntry:\n    from utils.error_capture import initialize_error_capture\n    # Initialize error capture with errors.log file\n    _error_log_file = os.getenv(\"ERROR_LOG_FILE\", \"errors.log\")\n    initialize_error_capture(_error_log_file)\nexcept Exception:\n    # If error capture fails to initialize, continue without it\n    # This ensures the application can still start\n    pass\n\n\ndef setup_logging(\n    log_level: Optional[str] = None,\n    log_file: Optional[str] = None,\n    log_format: Optional[str] = None\n):\n    \"\"\"\n    Set up logging configuration.\n    \n    Args:\n        log_level: Logging level (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL)\n        log_file: Optional path to log file\n        log_format: Optional custom log format\n    \n    TODO: Implement logging configuration\n    \"\"\"\n    # Get log level from environment or use default\n    level = log_level or os.getenv(\"LOG_LEVEL\", \"INFO\").upper()\n    \n    # Convert string level to logging constant\n    numeric_level = getattr(logging, level, logging.INFO)\n    \n    # Default log format\n    if log_format is None:\n        log_format = (\n            \"%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - \"\n            \"%(filename)s:%(lineno)d - %(message)s\"\n        )\n    \n    # Configure root logger\n    root_logger = logging.getLogger()\n    root_logger.setLevel(numeric_level)\n    \n    # Remove existing handlers\n    root_logger.handlers = []",

```json
        "contents": "def monitor_cost_spikes_and_trigger_alerts():\n\n    Monitor cloud costs and automatically detect spikes, triggering alerts.\n    \n    This function addresses the pain point of unforeseen costs by:\n    1. Collecting real-time cloud costs\n    2. Comparing against historical averages to detect spikes\n    3. Monitoring sustained spikes over consecutive days\n    4. Checking against absolute cost thresholds\n    5. Automatically triggering alerts when anomalies are detected\n    \n    This allows engineers to investigate and take corrective actions\n    before costs spiral out of control.\n    \n    Returns:\n        Dictionary with monitoring results including alert counts\n    \"\"\"\n    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n    \n    try:\n        # Import required modules\n        from data_collection.cloud_metrics import get_cloud_costs\n        from anomaly_detection.threshold_detection import (\n            compare_cost_to_historical,\n            monitor_sustained_spikes,\n            check_thresholds\n        )\n        from config.settings import get_settings\n        \n        settings = get_settings()\n        if settings is None:\n            logger.warning(\"Settings not available, skipping cost spike monitoring\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'error': 'Settings not available'}\n        \n        # Check if cost spike monitoring is enabled\n        cost_monitoring_enabled = getattr(settings, 'cost_spike_monitoring_enabled', True)\n        if not cost_monitoring_enabled:\n            logger.debug(\"Cost spike monitoring disabled in settings\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'skipped': 'Monitoring disabled'}\n        \n        if not settings.enable_cloud_metrics:\n            logger.debug(\"Cloud metrics disabled, skipping cost spike monitoring\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'skipped': 'Cloud metrics disabled'}\n        \n        logger.info(\"Starting cost spike monitoring and alert detection...\")\n        \n        # Collect real-time cloud costs\n        try:\n            cloud_cost_data = get_cloud_costs(store_in_db=True)\n            cost_items = cloud_cost_data.get('cloud_cost', [])\n            total_cost = cloud_cost_data.get('total_cost', 0.0)\n            \n            if not cost_items:\n                logger.debug(\"No cloud cost data collected, skipping spike detection\")",

        "contents": "# Monitor/Drift Agent\n\nA comprehensive monitoring and anomaly detection agent for system metrics and cloud usage, with automated alerting and optional self-healing capabilities.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe Monitor/Drift Agent is designed to:\n- Collect system metrics (CPU, memory, disk, network) and cloud usage metrics\n- Detect anomalies using threshold-based and machine learning methods\n- Enforce policies for monitoring and alerting\n- Send alerts through multiple channels (email, Slack, SMS)\n- Optionally perform self-healing actions (auto-scaling, shutdown)\n\n## Project Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmonitor_drift_agent/\n├── api/                           # API endpoints for agent communication\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── metrics.py                 # API to collect system metrics\n│   ├── alerts.py                 # API to trigger and manage alerts\n│   └── policies.py               # API to manage policies\n├── data_collection/               # Modules related to data collection\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── system_metrics.py         # Logic for collecting system metrics\n│   ├── cloud_metrics.py          # Logic for collecting cloud usage metrics\n│   └── database.py               # Database interactions (PostgreSQL)\n├── anomaly_detection/             # Anomaly detection logic\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── threshold_detection.py   # Threshold-based anomaly detection\n│   ├── machine_learning.py       # ML-based detection (Isolation Forest, Autoencoders)\n│   └── alert_trigger.py          # Logic for triggering alerts based on anomalies\n├── policy_management/             # Policy enforcement logic\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── policy_definition.py      # Logic for defining and storing policies\n│   └── policy_enforcement.py     # Logic for enforcing policies\n├── alerting/                      # Modules related to alerts and notifications\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── alert_system.py           # Alerting system (email, Slack, SMS)",

        "contents": "\"\"\"\nLogic for triggering alerts based on detected anomalies.\n\nThis module provides functionality to trigger alerts when anomalies\nare detected by the anomaly detection system.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom typing import Dict, List, Optional\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\n\nclass AlertTrigger:\n    \"\"\"Handles alert triggering based on anomaly detection results.\"\"\"\n    \n    def __init__(self, alert_system=None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize alert trigger.\n        \n        Args:\n            alert_system: Reference to alerting system module\n        \"\"\"\n        self.alert_system = alert_system\n    \n    def trigger_alert(self, anomaly: Dict) -&gt; Dict:\n        \"\"\"\n        Trigger an alert for a detected anomaly.\n        \n        Args:\n            anomaly: Dictionary containing anomaly information\n        \n        Returns:\n            Dictionary containing created alert information\n        \n        TODO: Implement alert triggering logic\n        \"\"\"\n        # TODO: Determine alert severity based on anomaly\n        severity = self._determine_severity(anomaly)\n        \n        # TODO: Format alert message\n        message = self._format_alert_message(anomaly)\n        \n        # TODO: Create alert using alerting system\n        alert_data = {\n            \"alert_type\": \"anomaly\",\n            \"severity\": severity,\n            \"message\": message,\n            \"metadata\": {\n                \"anomaly\": anomaly,\n                \"detected_at\": anomaly.get(\"timestamp\", datetime.now().isoformat())\n            }\n        }\n        \n        if self.alert_system:\n            # TODO: Call alert_system.create_alert(alert_data)\n            pass\n        \n        return alert_data\n    \n    def trigger_batch_alerts(self, anomalies: List[Dict]) -&gt; List[Dict]:\n        \"\"\"",

        "contents": "\"\"\"\nCustom logging utility for Monitor/Drift Agent.\n\nThis module provides a custom logger wrapper with additional\nfunctionality for structured logging and context management.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport logging\nfrom typing import Optional, Dict, Any\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\n\nclass CustomLogger:\n    \"\"\"Custom logger with additional functionality.\"\"\"\n    \n    def __init__(self, name: str, logger: Optional[logging.Logger] = None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize custom logger.\n        \n        Args:\n            name: Logger name\n            logger: Optional existing logger instance\n        \"\"\"\n        self.name = name\n        self.logger = logger or logging.getLogger(name)\n        self.context: Dict[str, Any] = {}\n    \n    def set_context(self, **kwargs):\n        \"\"\"\n        Set context variables for logging.\n        \n        Args:\n            **kwargs: Context key-value pairs\n        \"\"\"\n        self.context.update(kwargs)\n    \n    def clear_context(self):\n        \"\"\"Clear all context variables.\"\"\"\n        self.context = {}\n    \n    def _format_message(self, message: str) -&gt; str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Format message with context.\n        \n        Args:\n            message: Log message\n        \n        Returns:\n            Formatted message string\n        \n        TODO: Implement message formatting with context\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.context:\n            context_str = \" | \".join([f\"{k}={v}\" for k, v in self.context.items()])\n            return f\"{message} | Context: {context_str}\"\n        return message\n    \n    def debug(self, message: str, **kwargs):\n        \"\"\"Log debug message.\"\"\"\n        self.logger.debug(self._format_message(message), **kwargs)\n    \n    def info(self, message: str, **kwargs):\n        \"\"\"Log info message.\"\"\"\n        self.logger.info(self._format_message(message), **kwargs)\n    \n    def warning(self, message: str, **kwargs):\n        \"\"\"Log warning message.\"\"\"",

        "contents": "class CustomLogger:\n\n    \n    def warning(self, message: str, **kwargs):\n        \"\"\"Log warning message.\"\"\"\n        self.logger.warning(self._format_message(message), **kwargs)\n    \n    def error(self, message: str, **kwargs):\n        \"\"\"Log error message.\"\"\"\n        self.logger.error(self._format_message(message), **kwargs)\n    \n    def critical(self, message: str, **kwargs):\n        \"\"\"Log critical message.\"\"\"\n        self.logger.critical(self._format_message(message), **kwargs)\n    \n    def log_metric(self, metric_name: str, value: float, **metadata):\n        \"\"\"\n        Log a metric with structured data.\n        \n        Args:\n            metric_name: Name of the metric\n            value: Metric value\n            **metadata: Additional metadata\n        \"\"\"\n        message = f\"Metric: {metric_name}={value}\"\n        if metadata:\n            metadata_str = \" | \".join([f\"{k}={v}\" for k, v in metadata.items()])\n            message = f\"{message} | {metadata_str}\"\n        self.info(message)\n    \n    def log_alert(self, alert_type: str, severity: str, message: str, **metadata):\n        \"\"\"\n        Log an alert with structured data.\n        \n        Args:\n            alert_type: Type of alert\n            severity: Alert severity\n            message: Alert message\n            **metadata: Additional metadata\n        \"\"\"\n        log_message = f\"Alert [{severity.upper()}] {alert_type}: {message}\"\n        if metadata:\n            metadata_str = \" | \".join([f\"{k}={v}\" for k, v in metadata.items()])\n            log_message = f\"{log_message} | {metadata_str}\"\n        \n        # Use appropriate log level based on severity\n        severity_levels = {\n            \"low\": self.info,\n            \"medium\": self.warning,\n            \"high\": self.error,\n            \"critical\": self.critical\n        }\n        log_func = severity_levels.get(severity.lower(), self.warning)\n        log_func(log_message)\n\n\ndef get_logger(name: str) -&gt; CustomLogger:\n    \"\"\"",
```

Step-by-step guide to set up the database without Docker:

## Complete step-by-step guide

### Step 1: Install PostgreSQL locally

1. Download PostgreSQL:
   - Go to: https://www.postgresql.org/download/windows/
   - Click "Download the installer"
   - Or use: https://www.enterprisedb.com/downloads/postgres-postgresql-downloads
   - Download the Windows x86-64 installer

2. Run the installer:
   - Double-click the downloaded file
   - Click "Next" through the wizard
   - Important: when asked for a password, set one for the `postgres` user (e.g., `postgres123`)
   - Keep the default port: `5432`
   - Keep the default locale
   - Click "Next" until installation completes
   - Uncheck "Launch Stack Builder" at the end
   - Click "Finish"

3. Verify installation:
   - Open PowerShell
   - Run:
   ```powershell
   psql --version
   ```
   - If you see a version number, PostgreSQL is installed

### Step 2: Create the database

1. Open SQL Shell (psql):
   - Press `Windows Key`
   - Type "SQL Shell" or "psql"
   - Click "SQL Shell (psql)"

2. Connect to PostgreSQL:
   - Press `Enter` for Server (default: localhost)
   - Press `Enter` for Database (default: postgres)
   - Press `Enter` for Port (default: 5432)
   - Press `Enter` for Username (default: postgres)
   - Enter the password you set during installation
   - You should see: `postgres=#`

3. Create the database and user:
   - Copy and paste these commands one by one:
   ```sql
   CREATE DATABASE monitor_drift;
   ```
   - Press Enter
   ```sql
   CREATE USER monitor_drift WITH PASSWORD 'password';
   ```
   - Press Enter
   ```sql
   GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE monitor_drift TO monitor_drift;
   ```
   - Press Enter
   ```sql
   \q
   ```
   - Press Enter to exit

### Step 3: Create the .env file

1. Navigate to your project folder:
   ```powershell
   cd "a:\MonitorDrift Agent"
   ```

2. Create the `.env` file:
   ```powershell
   New-Item -Path ".env" -ItemType File -Force
   ```

3. Open the `.env` file in Notepad:
   ```powershell
   notepad .env
   ```

4. Add this line (replace `postgres123` with your actual PostgreSQL password):
   ```env
   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres123@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
   ```
   - Replace `postgres123` with the password you set during PostgreSQL installation
   - If you used a different username, replace `postgres` with that username

5. Save and close Notepad (Ctrl+S, then close)

### Step 4: Install required Python packages

1. Open PowerShell in your project folder:
   ```powershell
   cd "a:\MonitorDrift Agent"
   ```

2. Install packages:
   ```powershell
   pip install python-dotenv psycopg2-binary
   ```

### Step 5: Test the connection

1. Run the application:
   ```powershell
   python -m api.main
   ```

2. Expected output:
   - You should see: `✓ Database initialized successfully - all schemas created`
   - If you see an error, check the next section

### Troubleshooting

If you see "password authentication failed":
- Check your `.env` file has the correct password
- Verify the password in SQL Shell:
  ```sql
  \password postgres
  ```
  (Enter new password twice, then update your `.env` file)

If you see "could not connect to server":
- Check if PostgreSQL is running:
  ```powershell
   Get-Service -Name postgresql*
   ```
- If it's stopped, start it:
  ```powershell
   Start-Service postgresql-x64-15
   ```
  (Replace `15` with your PostgreSQL version number)

If you see "database does not exist":
- Go back to Step 2 and create the database again

If you see "psycopg2 not available":
- Run: `pip install psycopg2-binary`

### Quick verification checklist

- [ ] PostgreSQL installed
- [ ] Database `monitor_drift` created
- [ ] User `monitor_drift` created
- [ ] `.env` file created with correct DATABASE_URL
- [ ] `python-dotenv` installed (`pip install python-dotenv`)
- [ ] `psycopg2-binary` installed (`pip install psycopg2-binary`)

### Final test command

Run this to test everything:
```powershell
cd "a:\MonitorDrift Agent"
python -m api.main
```

If you see `✓ Database initialized successfully`, you're done.

If you encounter an error, share the exact error message and I can help troubleshoot.

PostgreSQL isn't installed or isn't in your PATH. Options:

## Option 1: Check if PostgreSQL is installed (but not in PATH)

Run these commands to check:

```powershell
# Check if PostgreSQL service exists
Get-Service -Name postgresql* -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

# Check common installation paths
Test-Path "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL"
Test-Path "C:\Program Files (x86)\PostgreSQL"
```

If you see a service or the paths exist, PostgreSQL is installed but not in PATH. Skip to "Add PostgreSQL to PATH" below.

## Option 2: Install PostgreSQL (if not installed)

### Method A: Using the official installer

1. Download:
   - Go to: https://www.postgresql.org/download/windows/
   - Click "Download the installer"
   - Download the Windows x86-64 installer (e.g., `postgresql-15.x-x64-windows.exe`)

2. Install:
   - Run the installer
   - Click "Next" through the setup
   - When asked for a password, set one for the `postgres` user (remember it)
   - Keep port `5432`
   - Complete the installation
   - Important: check "Add PostgreSQL to PATH" if offered

3. Restart PowerShell after installation

### Method B: Using winget (Windows Package Manager)

```powershell
winget install PostgreSQL.PostgreSQL
```

Then restart PowerShell.

## Option 3: Add PostgreSQL to PATH (if already installed)

If PostgreSQL is installed but `psql` isn't found:

1. Find PostgreSQL installation:
   ```powershell
   Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
   Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files (x86)\PostgreSQL" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
   ```

2. Add to PATH (replace `15` with your version):
   ```powershell
   $postgresPath = "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\15\bin"
   $env:Path += ";$postgresPath"
   [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", $env:Path, [EnvironmentVariableTarget]::User)
   ```

3. Restart PowerShell and test:
   ```powershell
   psql --version
   ```

## Option 4: Use Python to create the database (no psql needed)

If you prefer not to use the command line, use Python:

1. Create a Python script to set up the database:
   ```powershell
   # Create setup_database.py
   @"
import psycopg2
import sys

try:
    # Connect to default postgres database
    conn = psycopg2.connect(
        host="localhost",
        port=5432,
        user="postgres",
        password=input("Enter PostgreSQL password for 'postgres' user: "),
        database="postgres"
    )
    
    conn.autocommit = True
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Create database
    cursor.execute("CREATE DATABASE monitor_drift;")
    print("✓ Database 'monitor_drift' created")
    
    # Create user
    try:
        cursor.execute("CREATE USER monitor_drift WITH PASSWORD 'password';")
        print("✓ User 'monitor_drift' created")
    except:
        print("⚠ User 'monitor_drift' already exists (skipping)")
    
    # Grant privileges
    cursor.execute("GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE monitor_drift TO monitor_drift;")
    print("✓ Privileges granted")
    
    cursor.close()
    conn.close()
    print("\n✓ Database setup complete!")
    
except psycopg2.OperationalError as e:
    print(f"\n✗ Error: {e}")
    print("\nPossible issues:")
    print("1. PostgreSQL is not running")
    print("2. Wrong password")
    print("3. PostgreSQL is not installed")
    sys.exit(1)
except ImportError:
    print("\n✗ Error: psycopg2 not installed")
    print("Run: pip install psycopg2-binary")
    sys.exit(1)
"@ | Out-File -FilePath "setup_database.py" -Encoding UTF8
   ```

2. Run the script:
   ```powershell
   python setup_database.py
   ```

3. Enter your PostgreSQL password when prompted

## Quick check: Is PostgreSQL service running?

Check if PostgreSQL is installed and running:

```powershell
Get-Service -Name postgresql* | Format-Table -AutoSize
```

- If you see a service: PostgreSQL is installed. Start it if stopped:
  ```powershell
  Start-Service postgresql-x64-15
  ```
  (Replace `15` with your version)

- If you see nothing: PostgreSQL is not installed. Use Option 2 to install it.

## Recommended next steps

1. Check if PostgreSQL service exists:
   ```powershell
   Get-Service -Name postgresql*
   ```

2. If it exists:
   - Start the service (if stopped)
   - Use Option 4 (Python script) to create the database

3. If it doesn't exist:
   - Install PostgreSQL using Option 2
   - Then use Option 4 to create the database

Which option do you want to use? Share the output of `Get-Service -Name postgresql*` and I can provide exact steps.

## Option 1: Add PostgreSQL to PATH (to use psql)

## Option 2: Use Python script (recommended, no PATH needed)

Since PostgreSQL is running, create and run a Python script to set up the database:

### Step 1: Create the setup script

```powershell
cd "a:\MonitorDrift Agent"

@"
import psycopg2
import sys

print("Setting up database for Monitor/Drift Agent...")
print("=" * 50)

try:
    # Get password from user
    password = input("\nEnter PostgreSQL password for 'postgres' user: ")
    
    # Connect to default postgres database
    print("\nConnecting to PostgreSQL...")
    conn = psycopg2.connect(
        host="localhost",
        port=5432,
        user="postgres",
        password=password,
        database="postgres"
    )
    
    conn.autocommit = True
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Check if database exists
    cursor.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='monitor_drift'")
    if cursor.fetchone():
        print("⚠ Database 'monitor_drift' already exists")
        response = input("Do you want to recreate it? (yes/no): ")
        if response.lower() == 'yes':
            cursor.execute("DROP DATABASE monitor_drift;")
            print("✓ Old database dropped")
        else:
            print("Keeping existing database")
    
    # Create database
    if not cursor.fetchone():
        cursor.execute("CREATE DATABASE monitor_drift;")
        print("✓ Database 'monitor_drift' created")
    else:
        cursor.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='monitor_drift'")
        if not cursor.fetchone():
            cursor.execute("CREATE DATABASE monitor_drift;")
            print("✓ Database 'monitor_drift' created")
    
    # Create user
    try:
        cursor.execute("CREATE USER monitor_drift WITH PASSWORD 'password';")
        print("✓ User 'monitor_drift' created")
    except psycopg2.errors.DuplicateObject:
        print("⚠ User 'monitor_drift' already exists (skipping)")
    
    # Grant privileges
    cursor.execute("GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE monitor_drift TO monitor_drift;")
    print("✓ Privileges granted")
    
    cursor.close()
    conn.close()
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 50)
    print("✓ Database setup complete!")
    print("\nNext steps:")
    print("1. Create a .env file with:")
    print("   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:YOUR_PASSWORD@localhost:5432/monitor_drift")
    print("   (Replace YOUR_PASSWORD with the password you just entered)")
    print("\n2. Or use:")
    print("   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://monitor_drift:password@localhost:5432/monitor_drift")
    
except psycopg2.OperationalError as e:
    print(f"\n✗ Connection Error: {e}")
    print("\nPossible issues:")
    print("1. Wrong password - try again")
    print("2. PostgreSQL service is not running")
    print("3. Firewall blocking connection")
    sys.exit(1)
except ImportError:
    print("\n✗ Error: psycopg2 not installed")
    print("Run: pip install psycopg2-binary")
    sys.exit(1)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"\n✗ Unexpected error: {e}")
    sys.exit(1)
"@ | Out-File -FilePath "setup_database.py" -Encoding UTF8
```

### Step 2: Install psycopg2 (if not already installed)

```powershell
pip install psycopg2-binary
```

### Step 3: Run the setup script

```powershell
python setup_database.py
```

Enter your PostgreSQL password when prompted (the one you set during installation).

### Step 4: Create .env file

After the script completes, create the `.env` file:

```powershell

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:YOUR_PASSWORD@localhost:5432/monitor_drift
"@ | Out-File -FilePath ".env" -Encoding UTF8
```

Replace `YOUR_PASSWORD` with the password you entered in the script.

Or use the monitor_drift user:

## Method 1: Add PostgreSQL to PATH via PowerShell (quick)

Run these commands in PowerShell:

```powershell
# Add PostgreSQL 16 bin directory to PATH
$postgresPath = "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\bin"
$currentPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User")
if ($currentPath -notlike "*$postgresPath*") {
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "$currentPath;$postgresPath", "User")
    Write-Host "✓ PostgreSQL added to PATH" -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
    Write-Host "✓ PostgreSQL already in PATH" -ForegroundColor Green
}

# Refresh current session PATH
$env:Path += ";$postgresPath"

# Test if it works
Write-Host "`nTesting psql command..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
psql --version
```

If you see a version number, it worked.

## Method 2: Add PostgreSQL to PATH via GUI (manual)

1. Open System Properties:
   - Press `Windows Key + R`
   - Type: `sysdm.cpl`
   - Press Enter

2. Go to Environment Variables:
   - Click the "Advanced" tab
   - Click "Environment Variables..." at the bottom

3. Edit PATH:
   - Under "User variables", find "Path"
   - Click "Edit..."
   - Click "New"
   - Add: `C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\bin`
   - Click "OK" on all dialogs

4. Restart PowerShell:
   - Close and reopen PowerShell
   - Test: `psql --version`

## Method 3: Verify and add if missing

Run this to check and add if needed:

```powershell
# Check if PostgreSQL is already in PATH
$postgresPath = "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\bin"
$userPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User")

if ($userPath -like "*PostgreSQL*16*bin*") {
    Write-Host "✓ PostgreSQL is already in PATH" -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
    Write-Host "Adding PostgreSQL to PATH..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    $newPath = if ($userPath) { "$userPath;$postgresPath" } else { $postgresPath }
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", $newPath, "User")
    Write-Host "✓ PostgreSQL added to PATH" -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "`n⚠ Please restart PowerShell for changes to take effect" -ForegroundColor Yellow
}

# Add to current session
$env:Path += ";$postgresPath"

# Test
Write-Host "`nTesting psql..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
try {
    $version = psql --version 2>&1
    Write-Host "✓ Success! $version" -ForegroundColor Green
} catch {
    Write-Host "✗ psql not found. Please restart PowerShell and try again." -ForegroundColor Red
}
```

- If it says "Stopped": Service is stopped (go to Step 3)

## Step 2: If service is Running but connection fails

Try connecting with the service name:


```powershell

netstat -an | findstr 5432
```

If you see nothing, PostgreSQL isn't listening on that port.

## Step 3: Start the PostgreSQL service

```powershell
Get-Service -Name postgresql-x64-16
```

Status should be "Running".

```powershell
psql -U postgres
```


2. Check if PostgreSQL is configured to listen on localhost:
   ```powershell
   Get-Content "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\data\pg_hba.conf" | Select-String "localhost"
   ```

If the service fails to start, check the logs:


Or check PostgreSQL log file:

```powershell
import psycopg2

    # Grant privileges
    cursor.execute("GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE monitor_drift TO monitor_drift;")
    print("✓ Privileges granted")
    
    cursor.close()

except Exception as e:
    print(f"\n✗ Error: {e}")
```

Removing the redundant `urlparse` import on line 312. It's already imported at the module level, and the local import makes Python treat it as a local variable, causing the error.

Here's the fix - update the file:

**File: `a:\MonitorDrift Agent\data_collection\database.py`**

**Change line 310-317 from:**
```python
            if settings:
                try:
                    from urllib.parse import urlparse
                    parsed = urlparse(settings.database_url)
                    if parsed.username:
                        print(f"  Attempting to connect as user: {parsed.username}")
                except Exception:
                    pass
```

**To:**
```python
            if settings:
                try:
                    # urlparse is already imported at module level
                    parsed = urlparse(settings.database_url)
                    if parsed.username:
                        print(f"  Attempting to connect as user: {parsed.username}")
                except Exception:
                    pass
```

The issue: the `from urllib.parse import urlparse` on line 312 makes Python treat `urlparse` as a local variable throughout the function, so when line 278 uses it, Python thinks it's unassigned.

**Quick fix:** Remove line 312 (`from urllib.parse import urlparse`) since `urlparse` is already imported at the top of the file (line 11).

After making this change, run:
```powershell
python -m api.main
```

The database connection should work.

```json
        "contents": "def create_cloud_resource_costs_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n\n        cursor.close()\n        \n        return True\n    \n    except Error as e:\n        print(f\"Error creating cloud_resource_costs schema: {e}\")\n        if conn:\n            conn.rollback()\n        return False\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error creating cloud_resource_costs schema: {e}\")\n        if conn:\n            conn.rollback()\n        return False\n\n\ndef create_model_performance_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Create the database schema for storing ML model performance metrics.\n    \n    Creates a table called model_performance with columns for tracking\n    model performance metrics such as accuracy, detection rate, and alert rate.\n    \n    Args:\n        conn: psycopg2 connection object\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if schema creation successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    if conn is None:\n        print(\"Error: Database connection is None\")\n        return False\n    \n    try:\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Create model_performance table\n        create_table_query = \"\"\"\n        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS model_performance (\n            id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n            model_version TEXT,\n            total_predictions INTEGER NOT NULL,\n            anomalies_detected INTEGER NOT NULL,\n            alerts_triggered INTEGER NOT NULL,\n            avg_anomaly_score NUMERIC,\n            detection_rate NUMERIC NOT NULL,\n            alert_rate NUMERIC,\n            false_positive_rate NUMERIC,\n            evaluation_period_start TIMESTAMP,\n            evaluation_period_end TIMESTAMP,\n            timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n        );\n        ",

        "contents": "def monitor_cost_spikes_and_trigger_alerts():\n\n    Monitor cloud costs and automatically detect spikes, triggering alerts.\n    \n    This function addresses the pain point of unforeseen costs by:\n    1. Collecting real-time cloud costs\n    2. Comparing against historical averages to detect spikes\n    3. Monitoring sustained spikes over consecutive days\n    4. Checking against absolute cost thresholds\n    5. Automatically triggering alerts when anomalies are detected\n    \n    This allows engineers to investigate and take corrective actions\n    before costs spiral out of control.\n    \n    Returns:\n        Dictionary with monitoring results including alert counts\n    \"\"\"\n    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n    \n    try:\n        # Import required modules\n        from data_collection.cloud_metrics import get_cloud_costs\n        from anomaly_detection.threshold_detection import (\n            compare_cost_to_historical,\n            monitor_sustained_spikes,\n            check_thresholds\n        )\n        from config.settings import get_settings\n        \n        settings = get_settings()\n        if settings is None:\n            logger.warning(\"Settings not available, skipping cost spike monitoring\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'error': 'Settings not available'}\n        \n        # Check if cost spike monitoring is enabled\n        cost_monitoring_enabled = getattr(settings, 'cost_spike_monitoring_enabled', True)\n        if not cost_monitoring_enabled:\n            logger.debug(\"Cost spike monitoring disabled in settings\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'skipped': 'Monitoring disabled'}\n        \n        if not settings.enable_cloud_metrics:\n            logger.debug(\"Cloud metrics disabled, skipping cost spike monitoring\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'skipped': 'Cloud metrics disabled'}\n        \n        logger.info(\"Starting cost spike monitoring and alert detection...\")\n        \n        # Collect real-time cloud costs\n        try:\n            cloud_cost_data = get_cloud_costs(store_in_db=True)\n            cost_items = cloud_cost_data.get('cloud_cost', [])\n            total_cost = cloud_cost_data.get('total_cost', 0.0)\n            \n            if not cost_items:\n                logger.debug(\"No cloud cost data collected, skipping spike detection\")",

bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Create the database schema for storing alerts.\n    \n    Creates a table called alerts with columns for metric_name, value,\n    timestamp, resource_type, severity, and action_taken.\n    Also handles migration for existing tables by adding missing columns.\n    \n    Args:\n        conn: psycopg2 connection object\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if schema creation successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    if conn is None:\n        print(\"Error: Database connection is None\")\n        return False\n    \n    try:\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Create table with new schema (if table doesn't exist)\n        create_table_query = \"\"\"\n        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alerts (\n            id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n            metric_name TEXT NOT NULL,\n            value NUMERIC NOT NULL,\n            timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n            resource_type TEXT NOT NULL,\n            severity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium',\n            action_taken TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Alert Triggered'\n        );\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        cursor.execute(create_table_query)\n        conn.commit()\n        \n        # Migration: Add columns if they don't exist (for existing tables)\n        migration_query = \"\"\"\n        DO $$\n        BEGIN\n            IF NOT EXISTS (\n                SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns \n                WHERE table_name='alerts' AND column_name='severity'\n            ) THEN\n                ALTER TABLE alerts ADD COLUMN severity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium';\n            END IF;\n            \n            IF NOT EXISTS (\n                SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns \n                WHERE table_name='alerts' AND column_name='action_taken'\n            ) THEN\n                ALTER TABLE alerts ADD COLUMN action_taken TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Alert Triggered';\n            END IF;\n        END $$;\n        ",

        "contents": "def check_duplicate_metrics(\n    timestamp: datetime,\n    resource_type: str,\n    table_name: str = 'cloud_server_metrics'\n) -&gt; bool:\n\n        \n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Query to check for duplicates\n        # Use a small time window (e.g., 1 second) to account for slight timestamp differences\n        # This ensures we catch duplicates even if timestamps differ by milliseconds\n        query = \"\"\"\n            SELECT COUNT(*) \n            FROM {} \n            WHERE resource_type = %s \n            AND timestamp &gt;= %s - INTERVAL '1 second'\n            AND timestamp &lt;= %s + INTERVAL '1 second'\n        \"\"\".format(table_name)\n        \n        params = [resource_type, timestamp, timestamp]\n        \n        cursor.execute(query, params)\n        count = cursor.fetchone()[0]\n        \n        cursor.close()\n        \n        # Return True if duplicate exists (count &gt; 0)\n        return count &gt; 0\n    \n    except Error as e:\n        print(f\"Error checking for duplicate metrics: {e}\")\n        return False\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error checking for duplicate metrics: {e}\")\n        return False\n    finally:\n        # Ensure cursor and connection are closed\n        if cursor:\n            cursor.close()",

        "contents": "@router.get(\"/api/metrics\")\n@apply_rate_limit\nasync def get_metrics(request: Request):\n    \"\"\"\n    Retrieve the most recent system metrics (CPU, memory, network).\n    \n    This endpoint is rate-limited based on configuration.\n    \n    Returns:\n        JSON response containing:\n            - cpu_usage: CPU metrics dictionary\n            - memory_usage: Memory metrics dictionary\n            - network_traffic: Network metrics dictionary\n            - timestamp: ISO format timestamp\n    \n    Raises:\n        HTTPException: 500 if metric collection fails\n        RateLimitExceeded: 429 if rate limit is exceeded (handled by main.py)\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        # Collect all metrics\n        cpu_data = get_cpu_usage()\n        memory_data = get_memory_usage()\n        network_data = get_network_traffic()\n        \n        # Get unified timestamp\n        current_timestamp = datetime.now().isoformat()\n        \n        # Return structured JSON response\n        return {\n            \"cpu_usage\": cpu_data,\n            \"memory_usage\": memory_data,\n            \"network_traffic\": network_data,\n            \"timestamp\": current_timestamp\n        }\n    \n    except RuntimeError as e:\n        # Handle runtime errors (e.g., psutil not available)\n        raise HTTPException(\n            status_code=500,\n            detail=f\"Failed to collect metrics: {str(e)}\"\n        )\n    except Exception as e:\n        # Handle any other unexpected errors\n        raise HTTPException(\n            status_code=500,\n            detail=f\"Unexpected error collecting metrics: {str(e)}\"\n        )\n\n\n# Legacy functions kept for backward compatibility\ndef get_metrics_legacy(metric_type: Optional[str] = None) -&gt; Dict:\n    \"\"\"",

        "contents": "def connect_to_db():\n\n                try:\n                    # urlparse is already imported at module level\n                    parsed = urlparse(settings.database_url)\n                    if parsed.username:\n                        print(f\"  Attempting to connect as user: {parsed.username}\")\n                except Exception:\n                    pass\n        else:\n            print(f\"Error connecting to database: {e}\")\n        return None\n    except (ValueError, AttributeError) as e:\n        print(f\"Error parsing database URL: {e}\")\n        return None\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error connecting to database: {e}\")\n        return None\n\n\ndef create_cloud_metrics_schema(conn) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Create the database schema for storing cloud metrics.\n    \n    Creates a table called cloud_metrics with columns for provider,\n    metric_name, metric_value, timestamp, and resource_type.\n    \n    Args:\n        conn: psycopg2 connection object\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if schema creation successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    if conn is None:\n        print(\"Error: Database connection is None\")\n        return False\n    \n    try:\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Create cloud_metrics table\n        create_table_query = \"\"\"\n        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cloud_metrics (\n            id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n            provider TEXT NOT NULL,\n            metric_name TEXT NOT NULL,\n            metric_value NUMERIC,\n            timestamp TIMESTAMP,\n            resource_type TEXT NOT NULL\n        );\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        cursor.execute(create_table_query)\n        conn.commit()\n        cursor.close()\n        \n        return True",
```

Ways to store data and check it manually:

Method 1: Store data via API (recommended)

Step 1: Start the API server
```powershell
python -m api.main
```
Keep this running in one terminal window.

Step 2: Store data using API endpoint
Open a new PowerShell window and run:

```powershell
# Collect and store metrics via API
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/metrics/collect
```

Or using PowerShell's Invoke-WebRequest:

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://localhost:8000/api/metrics/collect" -Method POST
```

Method 2: Store data using Python script

Create a simple script to store test data:

```powershell
cd "a:\MonitorDrift Agent"

# Create a test script
@"
from data_collection.system_metrics import get_cpu_usage, get_memory_usage, get_network_traffic
from data_collection.database import store_metrics

# Collect current system metrics
print("Collecting system metrics...")
cpu_data = get_cpu_usage()
memory_data = get_memory_usage()
network_data = get_network_traffic()

print(f"CPU: {cpu_data['cpu_percent']}%")
print(f"Memory: {memory_data.get('percent', 'N/A')}%")
print(f"Network: {network_data.get('bytes_sent', 0)} bytes sent")

# Store in database
print("\nStoring metrics in database...")
success = store_metrics(cpu_data, memory_data, network_data)

if success:
    print("✓ Metrics stored successfully!")
else:
    print("✗ Failed to store metrics")
"@ | Out-File -FilePath "store_test_data.py" -Encoding UTF8

# Run the script
python store_test_data.py
```

Method 3: Check data manually using psql

Step 1: Connect to the database
```powershell
psql -U postgres -d monitor_drift
```
Enter your password when prompted.

Step 2: View all tables
```sql
\dt
```
This lists all tables.

Step 3: Query system_metrics table
```sql
-- View all system metrics
SELECT * FROM system_metrics ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 10;
```

Step 4: Query specific metrics
```sql
-- View only CPU metrics
SELECT id, cpu_usage, timestamp, resource_type 
FROM system_metrics 
WHERE resource_type = 'CPU' 
ORDER BY timestamp DESC 
LIMIT 10;

-- View only Memory metrics
SELECT id, memory_usage, timestamp, resource_type 
FROM system_metrics 
WHERE resource_type = 'Memory' 
ORDER BY timestamp DESC 
LIMIT 10;

-- Count total records
SELECT COUNT(*) as total_records FROM system_metrics;

-- View latest metrics
SELECT * FROM system_metrics 
ORDER BY timestamp DESC 
LIMIT 5;
```

Step 5: Check other tables
```sql
-- View alerts table
SELECT * FROM alerts ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 10;

-- View cloud_metrics table
SELECT * FROM cloud_metrics ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 10;

-- View cloud_server_metrics (unified metrics)
SELECT * FROM cloud_server_metrics ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 10;
```

Step 6: Exit psql
```sql
\q
```

Quick test — complete example

Run this to store data and verify:

```powershell
cd "a:\MonitorDrift Agent"

# 1. Store test data
python -c "
from data_collection.system_metrics import get_cpu_usage, get_memory_usage, get_network_traffic
from data_collection.database import store_metrics

cpu = get_cpu_usage()
memory = get_memory_usage()
network = get_network_traffic()

print('Storing metrics...')
if store_metrics(cpu, memory, network):
    print('✓ Data stored successfully!')
else:
    print('✗ Failed to store data')
"

# 2. Check data in database
psql -U postgres -d monitor_drift -c "SELECT COUNT(*) as total_records FROM system_metrics;"
psql -U postgres -d monitor_drift -c "SELECT * FROM system_metrics ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 5;"
```

Useful SQL queries for checking data

```sql
-- Connect to database first
psql -U postgres -d monitor_drift

-- Then run these queries:

-- 1. View all tables and their row counts
SELECT 
    schemaname,
    tablename,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.tables t2 WHERE t2.table_name = t1.tablename) as row_count
FROM pg_tables t1
WHERE schemaname = 'public'
ORDER BY tablename;

-- 2. View recent system metrics with details
SELECT 
    id,
    cpu_usage,
    memory_usage,
    network_traffic,
    timestamp,
    resource_type
FROM system_metrics
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 20;

-- 3. View metrics by resource type
SELECT 
    resource_type,
    COUNT(*) as count,
    MAX(timestamp) as latest_timestamp
FROM system_metrics
GROUP BY resource_type;

-- 4. View alerts (if any)
SELECT * FROM alerts ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 10;

-- 5. View all tables
\dt

-- 6. View table structure
\d system_metrics
\d alerts
\d cloud_metrics
```

Summary

1. Store data:
   - API: `POST http://localhost:8000/api/metrics/collect`
   - Python: Use `store_metrics()` function
   - Script: Run `store_test_data.py`

2. Check data manually:
   - Connect: `psql -U postgres -d monitor_drift`
   - Query: `SELECT * FROM system_metrics ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 10;`
   - Exit: `\q`

Start with Method 2 (Python script) to store test data, then use psql to verify.

## Method 1: Store data using Python script (recommended)

Create and run this script:

```powershell
cd "a:\MonitorDrift Agent"

# Create script to store metrics
@"
from data_collection.system_metrics import get_cpu_usage, get_memory_usage, get_network_traffic
from data_collection.database import store_metrics

print("Collecting system metrics...")
cpu_data = get_cpu_usage()
memory_data = get_memory_usage()
network_data = get_network_traffic()

print(f"CPU Usage: {cpu_data['cpu_percent']}%")
print(f"Memory Usage: {memory_data.get('percent', 'N/A')}%")
print(f"Network - Bytes Sent: {network_data.get('bytes_sent', 0)}")

print("\nStoring metrics in database...")
success = store_metrics(cpu_data, memory_data, network_data)

if success:
    print("✓ Metrics stored successfully in database!")
    print("\nYou can now check the data using:")
    print("  psql -U postgres -d monitor_drift -c \"SELECT * FROM system_metrics ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 5;\"")
else:

"@ | Out-File -FilePath "store_metrics.py" -Encoding UTF8

# Run the script

```

## Method 2: Check data manually using psql

After storing data, check it:

```powershell
# Connect to database
psql -U postgres -d monitor_drift
```

Then run these SQL queries:

```sql
-- View all recent metrics
SELECT * FROM system_metrics ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 10;

-- View only CPU metrics
SELECT id, cpu_usage, timestamp, resource_type 
FROM system_metrics 
WHERE resource_type = 'CPU' 
ORDER BY timestamp DESC 
LIMIT 10;

-- Count total records
SELECT COUNT(*) as total_records FROM system_metrics;

-- View metrics by type
SELECT resource_type, COUNT(*) as count 
FROM system_metrics 
GROUP BY resource_type;

-- Exit
\q
```

## Method 3: Quick one-liner to store and check

```powershell
# Store data
python -c "from data_collection.system_metrics import get_cpu_usage, get_memory_usage, get_network_traffic; from data_collection.database import store_metrics; store_metrics(get_cpu_usage(), get_memory_usage(), get_network_traffic()) and print('✓ Stored!')"

# Check data
psql -U postgres -d monitor_drift -c "SELECT * FROM system_metrics ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 5;"
```

```json
        "contents": "@router.get(\"/api/metrics\")\n@apply_rate_limit\nasync def get_metrics(request: Request):\n    \"\"\"\n    Retrieve the most recent system metrics (CPU, memory, network).\n    \n    This endpoint is rate-limited based on configuration.\n    \n    Returns:\n        JSON response containing:\n            - cpu_usage: CPU metrics dictionary\n            - memory_usage: Memory metrics dictionary\n            - network_traffic: Network metrics dictionary\n            - timestamp: ISO format timestamp\n    \n    Raises:\n        HTTPException: 500 if metric collection fails\n        RateLimitExceeded: 429 if rate limit is exceeded (handled by main.py)\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        # Collect all metrics\n        cpu_data = get_cpu_usage()\n        memory_data = get_memory_usage()\n        network_data = get_network_traffic()\n        \n        # Get unified timestamp\n        current_timestamp = datetime.now().isoformat()\n        \n        # Return structured JSON response\n        return {\n            \"cpu_usage\": cpu_data,\n            \"memory_usage\": memory_data,\n            \"network_traffic\": network_data,\n            \"timestamp\": current_timestamp\n        }\n    \n    except RuntimeError as e:\n        # Handle runtime errors (e.g., psutil not available)\n        raise HTTPException(\n            status_code=500,\n            detail=f\"Failed to collect metrics: {str(e)}\"\n        )\n    except Exception as e:\n        # Handle any other unexpected errors\n        raise HTTPException(\n            status_code=500,\n            detail=f\"Unexpected error collecting metrics: {str(e)}\"\n        )\n\n\n# Legacy functions kept for backward compatibility\ndef get_metrics_legacy(metric_type: Optional[str] = None) -&gt; Dict:\n    \"\"\"",

        "contents": "# Monitor/Drift Agent\n\nA comprehensive monitoring and anomaly detection agent for system metrics and cloud usage, with automated alerting and optional self-healing capabilities.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe Monitor/Drift Agent is designed to:\n- Collect system metrics (CPU, memory, disk, network) and cloud usage metrics\n- Detect anomalies using threshold-based and machine learning methods\n- Enforce policies for monitoring and alerting\n- Send alerts through multiple channels (email, Slack, SMS)\n- Optionally perform self-healing actions (auto-scaling, shutdown)\n\n## Project Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmonitor_drift_agent/\n├── api/                           # API endpoints for agent communication\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── metrics.py                 # API to collect system metrics\n│   ├── alerts.py                 # API to trigger and manage alerts\n│   └── policies.py               # API to manage policies\n├── data_collection/               # Modules related to data collection\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── system_metrics.py         # Logic for collecting system metrics\n│   ├── cloud_metrics.py          # Logic for collecting cloud usage metrics\n│   └── database.py               # Database interactions (PostgreSQL)\n├── anomaly_detection/             # Anomaly detection logic\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── threshold_detection.py   # Threshold-based anomaly detection\n│   ├── machine_learning.py       # ML-based detection (Isolation Forest, Autoencoders)\n│   └── alert_trigger.py          # Logic for triggering alerts based on anomalies\n├── policy_management/             # Policy enforcement logic\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── policy_definition.py      # Logic for defining and storing policies\n│   └── policy_enforcement.py     # Logic for enforcing policies\n├── alerting/                      # Modules related to alerts and notifications\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── alert_system.py           # Alerting system (email, Slack, SMS)",

        "contents": "@router.get(\"/api/metrics/cloud-and-server\")\n@apply_rate_limit\nasync def get_cloud_and_server_metrics(\n    timestamp: Optional[str] = None,\n    resource_type: Optional[str] = None,\n    metric_type: Optional[str] = None,\n    limit: int = 50,\n    offset: int = 0,\n    api_key_valid: bool = Depends(verify_api_key)\n) -&gt; Dict:\n    \"\"\"\n    Retrieve stored cloud and server metrics from the database.\n    \n    This endpoint retrieves metrics from the cloud_server_metrics table\n    with optional filtering by timestamp, resource_type, and metric_type.\n    Supports pagination via limit and offset parameters.\n    \n    Query Parameters:\n        timestamp: Optional ISO format timestamp string.         "contents": "def monitor_cost_spikes_and_trigger_alerts():\n\n    Monitor cloud costs and automatically detect spikes, triggering alerts.\n    \n    This function addresses the pain point of unforeseen costs by:\n    1. Collecting real-time cloud costs\n    2. Comparing against historical averages to detect spikes\n    3. Monitoring sustained spikes over consecutive days\n    4. Checking against absolute cost thresholds\n    5. Automatically triggering alerts when anomalies are detected\n    \n    This allows engineers to investigate and take corrective actions\n    before costs spiral out of control.\n    \n    Returns:\n        Dictionary with monitoring results including alert counts\n    \"\"\"\n    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n    \n    try:\n        # Import required modules\n        from data_collection.cloud_metrics import get_cloud_costs\n        from anomaly_detection.threshold_detection import (\n            compare_cost_to_historical,\n            monitor_sustained_spikes,\n            check_thresholds\n        )\n        from config.settings import get_settings\n        \n        settings = get_settings()\n        if settings is None:\n            logger.warning(\"Settings not available, skipping cost spike monitoring\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'error': 'Settings not available'}\n        \n        # Check if cost spike monitoring is enabled\n        cost_monitoring_enabled = getattr(settings, 'cost_spike_monitoring_enabled', True)\n        if not cost_monitoring_enabled:\n            logger.debug(\"Cost spike monitoring disabled in settings\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'skipped': 'Monitoring disabled'}\n        \n        if not settings.enable_cloud_metrics:\n            logger.debug(\"Cloud metrics disabled, skipping cost spike monitoring\")\n            return {'monitored': 0, 'alerts_triggered': 0, 'skipped': 'Cloud metrics disabled'}\n        \n        logger.info(\"Starting cost spike monitoring and alert detection...\")\n        \n        # Collect real-time cloud costs\n        try:\n            cloud_cost_data = get_cloud_costs(store_in_db=True)\n            cost_items = cloud_cost_data.get('cloud_cost', [])\n            total_cost = cloud_cost_data.get('total_cost', 0.0)\n            \n            if not cost_items:\n                logger.debug(\"No cloud cost data collected, skipping spike detection\")",

        "contents": "\"\"\"\nMain FastAPI application for Monitor/Drift Agent.\n\nThis module creates and configures the FastAPI application,\nincluding all routers and middleware.\n\"\"\"\n\n# Initialize error capture early to catch all terminal errors\ntry:\n    from utils.error_capture import initialize_error_capture\n    import os\n    _error_log_file = os.getenv(\"ERROR_LOG_FILE\", \"errors.log\")\n    initialize_error_capture(_error_log_file)\nexcept Exception:\n    # If error capture fails, continue without it\n    pass\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import JSONResponse\nfrom fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware\nfrom contextlib import asynccontextmanager\n\n# Try to import slowapi for rate limiting error handling\ntry:\n    from slowapi import Limiter, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler\n    from slowapi.errors import RateLimitExceeded\n    SLOWAPI_AVAILABLE = True\nexcept ImportError:\n    SLOWAPI_AVAILABLE = False\n    RateLimitExceeded = Exception\n\n# Import routers\nfrom api.metrics import router as metrics_router\nfrom api.policies import router as policies_router\n\n# Import settings\ntry:\n    from config.settings import get_settings\nexcept ImportError:\n    def get_settings():\n        return None\n\n\n@asynccontextmanager\nasync def lifespan(app: FastAPI):\n    \"\"\"\n    Lifespan context manager for FastAPI application.\n    \n    Handles startup and shutdown events:\n    -         "contents": "def collect_and_store_metrics() -&gt; bool:\n\n        return False\n\n\ndef collect_all_metrics() -&gt; Dict:\n    \"\"\"\n    Collect both server and cloud metrics into a unified structure.\n    \n    Coordinates collection of:\n    - Server metrics (CPU usage, memory usage)\n    - Cloud metrics (AWS, GCP, Azure)\n    \n    Returns:\n        Dictionary containing:\n            - timestamp: str (ISO format timestamp when collection started)\n            - server_metrics: Dict (CPU and memory usage with timestamp)\n            - cloud_metrics: Dict (AWS, GCP, Azure metrics by provider)\n    \n    Errors are handled gracefully - if a cloud provider is not configured\n    or fails, it will be omitted from results rather than causing failure.\n    \"\"\"\n    from utils.logger import get_logger\n    logger = get_logger(__name__)\n    \n    # Capture collection start timestamp (UTC)\n    collection_timestamp = datetime.utcnow()\n    \n    # Initialize result structure\n    result = {\n        'timestamp': collection_timestamp.isoformat(),\n        'server_metrics': {},\n        'cloud_metrics': {}\n    }\n    \n    # Collect server metrics\n    try:\n        result['server_metrics'] = get_server_metrics()\n        logger.info(\"Server metrics collected successfully\")\n    except RuntimeError as e:\n        logger.error(f\"Failed to collect server metrics: {str(e)}\")\n        result['server_metrics'] = {'error': str(e)}\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.error(f\"Unexpected error collecting server metrics: {str(e)}\", exc_info=True)\n        result['server_metrics'] = {'error': str(e)}\n    \n    # Collect cloud metrics - handle each provider independently\n    try:\n        from data_collection.cloud_metrics import get_aws_metrics, get_gcp_metrics, get_azure_metrics\n    except ImportError as e:\n        logger.warning(f\"Cloud metrics module not available: {str(e)}\")\n        result['cloud_metrics'] = {'error': 'Cloud metrics module not available'}\n        return result\n    \n    # Collect AWS metrics\n    try:\n        aws_metrics = get_aws_metrics()",

        "contents": "def store_metrics(cpu_data: Dict, memory_data: Dict, network_data: Dict) -&gt; bool:\n \"\"\"\n            INSERT INTO system_metrics (cpu_usage, memory_usage, network_traffic, timestamp, resource_type)\n            VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s);\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        # Insert CPU metric (check for duplicate first)\n        if check_duplicate_metrics(metric_timestamp, 'CPU', 'system_metrics'):\n            print(f\"Duplicate CPU metric detected for timestamp {metric_timestamp}. Skipping insert.\")\n        else:\n            cursor.execute(\n                insert_query,\n                (cpu_usage, None, None, metric_timestamp, 'CPU')\n            )\n        \n        # Insert Memory metric (check for duplicate first)\n        if check_duplicate_metrics(metric_timestamp, 'Memory', 'system_metrics'):\n            print(f\"Duplicate Memory metric detected for timestamp {metric_timestamp}.         "contents": "# Docker Compose configuration for Monitor/Drift Agent\nversion: '3.8'\n\nservices:\n  # Monitor/Drift Agent service\n  agent:\n    build:\n      context: ..\n      dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile\n    container_name: monitor_drift_agent\n    restart: unless-stopped\n    environment:\n      # Database configuration\n      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://monitor_drift:password@postgres:5432/monitor_drift\n      \n      # Metric collection settings\n      - METRIC_COLLECTION_INTERVAL=60\n      \n      # Threshold settings\n      - DEFAULT_CPU_THRESHOLD=80.0\n      - DEFAULT_MEMORY_THRESHOLD=80.0\n      - DEFAULT_DISK_THRESHOLD=80.0\n      \n      # Cloud provider credentials (set via .env file or secrets)\n      - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}\n      - AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}\n      - AWS_REGION=${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}\n      \n      # Alert channel configuration\n      - EMAIL_SMTP_SERVER=${EMAIL_SMTP_SERVER:-}\n      - EMAIL_SMTP_PORT=${EMAIL_SMTP_PORT:-587}\n      - EMAIL_USERNAME=${EMAIL_USERNAME:-}\n      - EMAIL_PASSWORD=${EMAIL_PASSWORD:-}\n      - SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}\n      \n      # Feature flags\n      - ANOMALY_DETECTION_ENABLED=true\n      - ML_DETECTION_ENABLED=false\n      - SELF_HEALING_ENABLED=false\n      \n      # API settings\n      - API_HOST=0.0.0.0\n      - API_PORT=8000\n      - API_DEBUG=false\n      \n      # Logging\n      - LOG_LEVEL=INFO\n    ports:\n      - \"8000:8000\"\n    volumes:\n      - ../logs:/app/logs\n      - ../data:/app/data\n    depends_on:\n      - postgres\n    networks:\n      - monitor_drift_network\n\n  # PostgreSQL database service\n  postgres:\n    image: postgres:15-alpine",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# Docker Compose configuration for Monitor/Drift Agent",
```

```json
        "contents": "\"\"\"\nLogic for logging alerts in the database.\n\nThis module provides functionality to log alerts to the database\nfor persistence and historical tracking.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom typing import Dict, List, Optional\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\n\nclass AlertLogger:\n    \"\"\"Handles logging of alerts to the database.\"\"\"\n    \n    def __init__(self, database=None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize alert logger.\n        \n        Args:\n            database: Optional database connection for logging\n        \"\"\"\n        self.database = database\n    \n    def log_alert(self, alert: Dict) -&gt; str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Log an alert to the database.\n        \n        Args:\n            alert: Dictionary containing alert information\n        \n        Returns:\n            Alert ID of logged alert\n        \n        TODO: Implement alert logging to database\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self.database:\n            # TODO: Log warning that database is not available\n            return \"\"\n        \n        # TODO: Prepare alert data for database insertion\n        alert_data = {\n            \"alert_id\": alert.get(\"alert_id\"),\n            \"alert_type\": alert.get(\"alert_type\"),\n            \"severity\": alert.get(\"severity\"),\n            \"message\": alert.get(\"message\"),\n            \"metadata\": alert.get(\"metadata\", {}),\n            \"status\": alert.get(\"status\", \"created\"),\n            \"created_at\": alert.get(\"timestamp\", datetime.now().isoformat()),\n            \"channels\": alert.get(\"channels\", {})\n        }\n        \n        # TODO: Insert alert into database\n        alert_id = self.database.insert_alert(alert_data)\n        \n        return alert_id\n    \n    def log_alert_batch(self, alerts: List[Dict]) -&gt; List[str]:\n        \"\"\"",

        "contents": "class AlertHistory:\n\n    \n    def search_alerts(self, query: str, limit: int = 100) -&gt; List[Dict]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Search alerts by message content or metadata.\n        \n        Args:\n            query: Search query string\n            limit: Maximum number of results to return\n        \n        Returns:\n            List of matching alert dictionaries\n        \n        TODO: Implement alert search functionality\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self.database:\n            return []\n        \n        # TODO: Implement search query\n        # This would typically involve full-text search in the database\n        all_alerts = self.list_alerts(limit=limit * 10)  # Get more to filter\n        \n        # Simple text search in message\n        matching_alerts = [\n            alert for alert in all_alerts\n            if query.lower() in alert.get(\"message\", \"\").lower()\n        ]\n        \n        return matching_alerts[:limit]\n\n\ndef get_alert_history(\n    severity: Optional[str] = None,\n    resource_type: Optional[str] = None,\n    time_range: Optional[Union[datetime, timedelta, int]] = None,\n    limit: int = 100,\n    offset: int = 0\n) -&gt; List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n    ",

        "contents": "@unittest.skipUnless(ALERTING_AVAILABLE, \"Alerting modules not available\")\nclass TestTriggerAlert(unittest.TestCase):\n@patch('data_collection.database.store_alert_in_db')\n    @patch('alerting.alert_system.determine_alert_channels')\n    @patch('alerting.alert_system.create_alert_system_from_settings')\ndef test_trigger_alert_sends_notifications(self, mock_create_system, mock_determine, mock_store):\n\n        \n        self.assertTrue(result)\n        mock_system.send_alert.assert_called_once()\n        call_args = mock_system.send_alert.call_args\n        self.assertEqual(call_args[1]['alert_type'], 'metric_alert')\n        self.assertIn('severity', call_args[1])\n    \n    def test_trigger_alert_invalid_inputs(self):\n        \"\"\"Test trigger_alert with invalid inputs\"\"\"\n        timestamp = datetime.utcnow()\n        \n        # Invalid metric_name\n        result = trigger_alert(\"\", 85.5, timestamp, \"Server\")\n        self.assertFalse(result)\n        \n        # Invalid value\n        result = trigger_alert(\"CPU Usage\", \"invalid\", timestamp, \"Server\")\n        self.assertFalse(result)\n        \n        # Invalid timestamp\n        result = trigger_alert(\"CPU Usage\", 85.5, \"invalid\", \"Server\")\n        self.assertFalse(result)\n        \n        # Invalid resource_type\n        result = trigger_alert(\"CPU Usage\", 85.5, timestamp, \"\")\n        self.assertFalse(result)\n    \n    @patch('data_collection.database.store_alert_in_db')\n    @patch('alerting.alert_system.determine_alert_channels')\n    @patch('alerting.alert_system.create_alert_system_from_settings')\n    def test_trigger_alert_handles_notification_failure(self, mock_create_system, mock_determine, mock_store):\n        ",

bool:\n    \"\"\"\n    Store unified metrics (server + cloud) in the cloud_server_metrics table.\n    \n    This function stores both server metrics and optional cloud metrics in\n    a single row in the unified cloud_server_metrics table.\n    \n    Args:\n        cpu_usage: Server CPU usage as percentage (required)\n        memory_usage: Server memory usage as percentage or bytes (required)\n        network_traffic: Server network bandwidth in bytes (required)\n        resource_type: Resource type identifier (Server, AWS, GCP, Azure) (required)\n        cloud_compute: Cloud compute usage (optional)\n        cloud_storage: Cloud storage usage (optional)\n        cloud_bandwidth: Cloud bandwidth usage (optional)\n        timestamp: Timestamp when metrics were collected (optional, defaults to current time)\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if storage successful, False otherwise\n    \"\"\"\n    conn = None\n    \n    try:\n        # Validate required parameters\n        if cpu_usage is None or memory_usage is None or network_traffic is None:\n            print(\"Error: cpu_usage, memory_usage, and network_traffic are required\")\n            return False\n        \n        if not resource_type:\n            print(\"Error: resource_type is required\")\n            return False\n        \n        # Validate resource_type\n        valid_resource_types = ['Server', 'AWS', 'GCP', 'Azure']\n        if resource_type not in valid_resource_types:\n            print(f\"Error: resource_type must be one of {valid_resource_types}\")\n            return False\n        \n        # Establish database connection\n        conn = connect_to_db()\n        if conn is None:\n            print(\"Failed to establish database connection\")\n            return False\n        \n        # Ensure schema exists\n        if",

        "contents": "def check_duplicate_cloud_metric(\n    timestamp: datetime,\n    provider: str,\n    metric_name: str,\n    resource_type: str\n) -&gt; bool:\n\"\"\"\n    Check if a cloud metric with the same timestamp, provider, metric_name, and resource_type already exists.\n    \n    This function queries the cloud_metrics table to check if a record with the same\n    timestamp, provider, metric_name, and resource_type already exists, helping prevent duplicate entries.\n    \n    Args:\n        timestamp: Timestamp to check for duplicates\n        provider: Cloud provider name (aws, gcp, azure)\n        metric_name: Name of the metric\n        resource_type: Resource type (Compute, Storage, Network)\n    \n    Returns:\n        True if duplicate exists, False otherwise\n    \n    Raises:\n        RuntimeError: If psycopg2 is not available\n    \"\"\"\n    if not PSYCOPG2_AVAILABLE:\n        raise RuntimeError(\n            \"psycopg2 library is not available. Please install it using: pip install psycopg2-binary\"\n        )\n    \n    conn = None\n    cursor = None\n    \n    try:\n        # Establish database connection\n        conn = connect_to_db()\n        if conn is None:\n            print(\"Failed to establish database connection for duplicate check\")\n            return False\n        \n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n        \n        # Query to check for duplicates in cloud_metrics table\n        # Use a small time window (e.g., 1 second) to account for slight timestamp differences\n        query = \"\"\"\n            SELECT COUNT(*) \n            FROM cloud_metrics \n            WHERE provider = %s \n            AND metric_name = %s \n            AND resource_type = %s \n            AND timestamp &gt;= %s - INTERVAL '1 second'\n            AND timestamp &lt;= %s + INTERVAL '1 second'\n        \"\"\"\n        \n        params = [provider, metric_name, resource_type, timestamp, timestamp]\n        \n        cursor.execute(query, params)\n        count = cursor.fetchone()[0]\n        \n        cursor.close()\n        \n        # Return True if duplicate exists (count &gt; 0)\n        return count &gt; 0\n    \n    except Error as e:\n        print(f\"Error checking for duplicate cloud metric: {e}\")\n        return False\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Unexpected error checking for duplicate cloud metric: {e}\")\n        return False\n    finally:\n        # Ensure cursor and connection are closed\n        if cursor:\n            cursor.close()\n        if conn:\n            conn.close()\n\n\ndef store_unified_metrics(\n    cpu_usage: float,\n    memory_usage: float,\n    network_traffic: float,\n    resource_type: str,\n    cloud_compute: Optional[float] = None,\n    cloud_storage: Optional[float] = None,\n    cloud_bandwidth: Optional[float] = None,\n    timestamp: Optional[datetime] = None\n) -&gt; bool:\n    ",

        "contents": "def get_alert_history(\n    severity: Optional[str] = None,\n    resource_type: Optional[str] = None,\n    time_range: Optional[Union[datetime, timedelta, int]] = None,\n    limit: int = 100,\n    offset: int = 0\n) -&gt; List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Retrieve alert history from the PostgreSQL database with optional filtering.\n    \n    This function queries the alerts table and returns a list of alert dictionaries\n    matching the specified filters. Results are ordered by timestamp (most recent first).\n    \n    Args:\n        severity: Optional filter by severity level (\"critical\", \"high\", \"medium\", \"low\")\n        resource_type: Optional filter by resource type (\"Server\", \"AWS\", \"GCP\", \"Azure\", \"Cloud\")\n        time_range: Optional time range filter. 80.0)\n- &#96;DEFAULT_DISK_THRESHOLD&#96;: Default disk usage threshold (default: 80.0)\n\n### Cloud Provider Credentials\n- AWS: &#96;AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID&#96;, &#96;AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY&#96;, &#96;AWS_REGION&#96;\n- Azure: &#96;AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID&#96;, &#96;AZURE_CLIENT_ID&#96;, &#96;AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET&#96;, &#96;AZURE_TENANT_ID&#96;\n- GCP: &#96;GCP_PROJECT_ID&#96;, &#96;GCP_CREDENTIALS_PATH&#96;\n\n### Alert Channels\n- Email: &#96;EMAIL_SMTP_SERVER&#96;, &#96;EMAIL_SMTP_PORT&#96;, &#96;EMAIL_USERNAME&#96;, &#96;EMAIL_PASSWORD&#96;\n- Slack:         "contents": "# Monitor/Drift Agent\n\nA comprehensive monitoring and anomaly detection agent for system metrics and cloud usage, with automated alerting and optional self-healing capabilities.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe Monitor/Drift Agent is designed to:\n- Collect system metrics (CPU, memory, disk, network) and cloud usage metrics\n- Detect anomalies using threshold-based and machine learning methods\n- Enforce policies for monitoring and alerting\n- Send alerts through multiple channels (email, Slack, SMS)\n- Optionally perform self-healing actions (auto-scaling, shutdown)\n\n## Project Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmonitor_drift_agent/\n├── api/                           # API endpoints for agent communication\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── metrics.py                 # API to collect system metrics\n│   ├── alerts.py                 # API to trigger and manage alerts\n│   └── policies.py               # API to manage policies\n├── data_collection/               # Modules related to data collection\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── system_metrics.py         # Logic for collecting system metrics\n│   ├── cloud_metrics.py          # Logic for collecting cloud usage metrics\n│   └── database.py               # Database interactions (PostgreSQL)\n├── anomaly_detection/             # Anomaly detection logic\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── threshold_detection.py   # Threshold-based anomaly detection\n│   ├── machine_learning.py       # ML-based detection (Isolation Forest, Autoencoders)\n│   └── alert_trigger.py          # Logic for triggering alerts based on anomalies\n├── policy_management/             # Policy enforcement logic\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── policy_definition.py      # Logic for defining and storing policies\n│   └── policy_enforcement.py     # Logic for enforcing policies\n├── alerting/                      # Modules related to alerts and notifications\n│   ├── __init__.py\n│   ├── alert_system.py           # Alerting system (email, Slack, SMS)",

        "contents": "class ResourcePolicy:\ndef validate(self) -&gt; bool:\n\n        \n        if self.threshold_type not in [\"usage\", \"cost\"]:\n            raise ValueError(\"threshold_type must be 'usage' or 'cost'\")\n        \n        if not isinstance(self.duration, int) or self.duration &lt; 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"duration must be a non-negative integer\")\n        \n        return True\n    \n    def to_dict(self) -&gt; Dict:\n        \"\"\"Convert policy to dictionary representation.\"\"\"\n        return {\n            \"policy_id\": self.policy_id,\n            \"resource_name\": self.resource_name,\n            \"threshold_value\": self.threshold_value,\n            \"threshold_type\": self.threshold_type,\n            \"duration\": self.duration,\n            \"enabled\": self.enabled,\n            \"created_at\": self.created_at.isoformat() if isinstance(self.created_at, datetime) else self.created_at,\n            \"updated_at\": self.updated_at.isoformat() if isinstance(self.updated_at, datetime) else self.updated_at\n        }\n    \n    def enable(self):\n        \"\"\"Enable the policy.\"\"\"\n        self.enabled = True\n        self.updated_at = datetime.utcnow()\n    \n    def disable(self):\n        \"\"\"Disable the policy.\"\"\"\n        self.enabled = False\n        self.updated_at = datetime.utcnow()\n\n\nclass PolicyDefinitionManager:\n    \"\"\"Manages policy definitions and storage.\"\"\"\n    \n    def __init__(self, database=None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize policy definition manager.\n        \n        Args:\n            database: Optional database connection for persistence\n        \"\"\"\n        self.database = database\n        self.policies: Dict[str, Policy] = {}",
```

## Implementation complete

### 1. Added POST /api/metrics/collect endpoint
- Collects current system metrics (CPU, memory, network)
- Stores them in the database
- Returns success status with collected metrics

### 2. Implemented alerts router
- GET /api/alerts — List alerts with filtering (severity, resource_type, time range, pagination)
- POST /api/alerts — Create new alert
- GET /api/alerts/{id} — Get specific alert by ID
- PUT /api/alerts/{id} — Update alert (action_taken)
- DELETE /api/alerts/{id} — Delete alert

### 3. Added policy management endpoints
- GET /api/policies — List all resource policies
- POST /api/policies — Create new resource policy
- GET /api/policies/{id} — Get specific policy by ID
- PUT /api/policies/{id} — Update policy
- DELETE /api/policies/{id} — Delete policy

### 4. Added database query function
- `get_alerts_from_db()` — Retrieves alerts with filtering and pagination

### 5. Included alerts router in main.py
- Alerts router is now registered and available

### 6. Created API documentation
- `API_ENDPOINTS.md` — Complete documentation with Postman examples

## All available endpoints for Postman

**Health & Info:**
- GET `/health` — Health check
- GET `/` — API info
- GET `/docs` — Swagger UI

**Metrics:**
- GET `/api/metrics` — Get current metrics
- POST `/api/metrics/collect` — Collect & store metrics
- GET `/api/metrics/cloud-and-server` — Get stored metrics

**Alerts:**
- GET `/api/alerts` — List alerts
- POST `/api/alerts` — Create alert
- GET `/api/alerts/{id}` — Get alert
- PUT `/api/alerts/{id}` — Update alert
- DELETE `/api/alerts/{id}` — Delete alert

**Policies:**
- GET `/api/policies/thresholds` — Get thresholds
- POST `/api/policies/thresholds` — Update thresholds
- GET `/api/policies` — List policies
- POST `/api/policies` — Create policy
- GET `/api/policies/{id}` — Get policy
- PUT `/api/policies/{id}` — Update policy
- DELETE `/api/policies/{id}` — Delete policy

## Quick test in Postman

1. Start the API:
   ```powershell
   python -m api.main
   ```

2. Test in Postman:
   - POST `http://localhost:8000/api/metrics/collect` — Store metrics
   - GET `http://localhost:8000/api/alerts` — View alerts
   - POST `http://localhost:8000/api/alerts` — Create alert
   - GET `http://localhost:8000/api/policies` — View policies

All endpoints are implemented and ready for Postman testing. See `API_ENDPOINTS.md` for detailed documentation with request/response examples.
